lessons.title: 233. Things I did in my life
lessons.subtitle: Escalé una montaña. Fui a un concierto. Doné sangre.

explanations.title: What have you done in your life?
explanations.body: To say what you did at some point in your life, use the preterite. Each of these sentences tells about a finished experience. Tap a row to hear it.

rows: Pasé un tiempo en el extranjero.
I learned to play an instrument.
Vi obras de arte en un museo.
I saw works of art in a museum.
Actué en una obra de teatro.

explanations.title: Asking about experiences
explanations.body: Ask with ¿Alguna vez…? (ever) and the preterite. To answer, say sí, una vez… or no, nunca. If nunca comes first, you drop no: Nunca escalé una montaña.

examples.text: ¿Alguna vez escalaste una montaña?
examples.translation: Have you ever climbed a mountain?

examples.text: Sí, una vez escalé una montaña muy alta.
examples.translation: Yes, once I climbed a very high mountain.

examples.text: No, nunca vi animales salvajes.
examples.translation: No, I never saw wild animals.

examples.text: ¿Alguna vez actuaste en una obra de teatro?
examples.translation: Did you ever act in a play?

explanations.title: Spelling in the yo form
explanations.body: Remember the spelling changes in the yo form of the preterite: tocar → toqué, practicar → practiqué, llegar → llegué, empezar → empecé. Verbs like escalar and donar are regular: escalé, doné.

examples.text: Practiqué un deporte durante muchos años.
examples.translation: I played a sport for many years.

examples.text: Llegué a la cima de la montaña.
examples.translation: I reached the top of the mountain.

exercises.prompt: Anoche yo ___ a un concierto con mi hermana.
exercises.promptTranslation: Last night I went to a concert with my sister.

exercises.prompt: Hace tres años yo ___ una montaña muy alta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Three years ago I climbed a very tall mountain.

exercises.prompt: En la universidad yo ___ sangre por primera vez.
exercises.promptTranslation: At the university I donated blood for the first time.

exercises.prompt: ¿Alguna vez ___ tú en una obra de teatro?
exercises.promptTranslation: Did you ever act in a play?

exercises.prompt: Mi hermano ___ a tocar la guitarra a los diez años.
exercises.promptTranslation: My brother learned to play the guitar at ten.

exercises.prompt: Ellos ___ un tiempo en el extranjero.
exercises.promptTranslation: They spent some time abroad.

exercises.prompt: What does “alguna vez” mean in a question?
Which sentence means “I climbed a mountain”?
How do you write “I practiced” (practicar, yo)?
exercises.explanation: C changes to qu before é to keep the k sound.

lessons.title: 234. The preterite: five jobs
lessons.subtitle: Me bañé y fui a trabajar. El hombre pasó tres días en el hospital.

explanations.title: What happened?
explanations.body: The preterite answers the question ¿Qué pasó? (What happened?). It moves the story forward. In this lesson you will see its five main jobs.

rows: Me bañé y fui a trabajar.
I showered and went to work.
Un hombre murió en el accidente.
A man died in the accident.
Primero el coche chocó y por último rodó.
First the car crashed and finally it rolled.
El hombre pasó tres días en el hospital.
The man spent three days at the hospital.
I was studying when I got your call.

explanations.title: Words that go with the preterite
explanations.body: Look for time words that mark one point or one period: ayer (yesterday), anoche (last night), la semana pasada, el año pasado, hace tres meses (three months ago), de repente (suddenly), en ese momento (at that moment), una vez (once).

examples.text: Ayer terminé mi trabajo a las cinco.
examples.translation: Yesterday I finished my work at five.

examples.text: La semana pasada viajamos a la costa.
examples.translation: Last week we traveled to the coast.

examples.text: De repente, alguien tocó a la puerta.
examples.translation: Suddenly, someone knocked on the door.

examples.text: Hace tres meses empecé a estudiar español.
examples.translation: Three months ago I began to study Spanish.

explanations.title: Stem changes
explanations.body: Stem changes in the preterite happen only in -ir verbs, and only in the él and ellos forms: prefirió, prefirieron; murió, murieron. The other forms keep the original vowel: preferí, preferiste, preferimos.

exercises.prompt: Ayer mi madre ___ el trabajo a las cinco.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday my mother finished work at five.

exercises.prompt: La semana pasada nosotros ___ a la costa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Last week we traveled to the coast.

exercises.prompt: Un hombre ___ en el accidente.
exercises.promptTranslation: A man died in the accident.

exercises.prompt: Los dos hombres ___ el hotel con vista al mar.
exercises.promptTranslation: The two men preferred the hotel with an ocean view.

exercises.prompt: Hace tres meses yo ___ a estudiar español.
exercises.promptTranslation: Three months ago I began to study Spanish.

exercises.prompt: El hombre ___ tres días en el hospital.
exercises.promptTranslation: The man spent three days in the hospital.

exercises.prompt: What does the preterite tell you about?
options: what was happening in the background
what used to happen every day
exercises.explanation: The preterite moves the story forward.

exercises.prompt: Which time word marks one finished moment?
exercises.explanation: Ayer = yesterday, one point in time.

exercises.prompt: In which forms does morir change its stem in the preterite?
exercises.explanation: Murió, murieron: only the third person.

lessons.title: 235. Preterite practice: regular, irregular, stem-changing
lessons.subtitle: Nos dieron un regalo. Tuvieron un hijo. Pedí una pizza.

explanations.title: Sort the verb first
explanations.body: Before you conjugate, decide which kind of verb it is. Regular verbs use -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -aron or -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -ieron. Irregular verbs have a new stem (tuv-, hic-, dij-, pud-). -ir verbs with a stem change switch the vowel in two forms (pidió, durmieron). Some forms have spelling changes (llegué, leyó).

explanations.title: Two verbs, one form
explanations.body: Ser and ir have exactly the same preterite forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. The rest of the sentence tells you which verb it is: Fue un día largo (ser) and Fue a la playa (ir).

examples.text: Fue un día muy largo.
examples.translation: It was a very long day.

examples.text: Fue a la playa con sus primos.
examples.translation: He went to the beach with his cousins.

exercises.prompt: Los estudiantes ___ mucha suerte en el examen.
exercises.promptTranslation: The students were very lucky on the exam.

exercises.prompt: Tú ___ muy bien la tarea.
exercises.promptTranslation: You did the homework very well.

exercises.prompt: Mi amiga ___ una pizza grande.
exercises.promptTranslation: My friend ordered a large pizza.

exercises.prompt: Los niños ___ nueve horas anoche.
exercises.promptTranslation: The children slept nine hours last night.

exercises.prompt: Yo le ___ las gracias a la maestra.
exercises.promptTranslation: I thanked the teacher.

exercises.prompt: Ella ___ el periódico en el tren.
exercises.promptTranslation: She read the newspaper on the train.

exercises.prompt: Ellos nos ___ la verdad.
exercises.promptTranslation: They told us the truth.

exercises.prompt: Yo no ___ ir a la fiesta.
exercises.promptTranslation: I could not go to the party.

exercises.prompt: How do you know “Fue a la playa” uses ir and not ser?
exercises.explanation: Ir takes a before a place.

lessons.title: 236. Famous lives
lessons.subtitle: Picasso nació en Málaga. García Márquez ganó el Premio Nobel.

explanations.title: Five short biographies
explanations.body: Biographies use the preterite for births, studies, works and prizes. Read each life and notice the verbs: nació, estudió, vivió, escribió, ganó, recibió.

examples.text: Pablo Picasso nació en Málaga en mil ochocientos ochenta y uno. Estudió arte en Madrid y Barcelona y vivió muchos años en Francia.
examples.translation: Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga in 1881. He studied art in Madrid and Barcelona and lived many years in France.

examples.text: Miguel de Cervantes escribió Don Quijote. Publicó la primera parte en mil seiscientos cinco.
examples.translation: Miguel de Cervantes wrote Don Quixote. He published the first part in 1605.

examples.text: Gabriel García Márquez nació en Aracataca, Colombia. Escribió Cien años de soledad y ganó el Premio Nobel de Literatura en mil novecientos ochenta y dos.
examples.translation: Gabriel García Márquez was born in Aracataca, Colombia. He wrote One Hundred Years of Solitude and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982.

examples.text: Frida Kahlo nació en Coyoacán, México. A los dieciocho años tuvo un accidente de autobús. Después aprendió a pintar.
examples.translation: Frida Kahlo was born in Coyoacán, Mexico. At eighteen she had a bus accident. Afterwards she learned to paint.

examples.text: Pablo Neruda recibió el Premio Nobel de Literatura en mil novecientos setenta y uno y murió en Santiago de Chile.
examples.translation: Pablo Neruda received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971 and died in Santiago, Chile.

explanations.title: Dates and ages in a life story
explanations.body: Use en + year for a date: en mil novecientos ochenta y dos. Use a los + number + años for an age: a los dieciocho años. Use hasta (until) for the end of a period: vivió en París hasta mil novecientos treinta.

rows: Nació en Málaga en mil ochocientos ochenta y uno.

exercises.prompt: Pablo Picasso ___ en Málaga.
exercises.promptTranslation: Pablo Picasso was born in Málaga.

exercises.prompt: Cervantes ___ Don Quijote.
exercises.promptTranslation: Cervantes wrote Don Quixote.

exercises.prompt: García Márquez ___ el Premio Nobel de Literatura.
exercises.promptTranslation: García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

exercises.prompt: Neruda ___ el Premio Nobel en mil novecientos setenta y uno.
exercises.promptTranslation: Neruda received the Nobel Prize in 1971.

exercises.prompt: Picasso ___ muchos años en Francia.
exercises.promptTranslation: Picasso lived many years in France.

exercises.prompt: Frida Kahlo ___ a pintar después del accidente.
exercises.promptTranslation: Frida Kahlo learned to paint after the accident.

exercises.prompt: Who wrote Don Quijote?
What did Frida Kahlo learn to do after her accident?
Which preposition marks an age, as in “a los dieciocho años”?
exercises.explanation: A los dieciocho años = at eighteen.

lessons.title: 237. Becoming and pretending: hacerse
lessons.subtitle: Mauricio se hizo abogado. Profesor, ¡no se haga!

explanations.title: Hacerse: to become
explanations.body: Hacer has many uses. One is hacerse, to become something through effort or choice: a profession, a religion, a rich or famous person. Conjugate it like hacer and keep the reflexive pronoun: me hice, te hiciste, se hizo.

examples.text: Mauricio se hizo abogado después de años de estudio.
examples.translation: Mauricio became a lawyer after years of study.

examples.text: Maricela se hizo rica al ganar la lotería.
examples.translation: Maricela became rich when she won the lottery.

examples.text: Mi hermana se hizo médica en Chile.
examples.translation: My sister became a doctor in Chile.

examples.text: Ellos se hicieron famosos con su primera canción.
examples.translation: They became famous with their first song.

explanations.title: Hacerse: to pretend
explanations.body: Hacerse also means to pretend. You often hear hacerse el tonto (to play dumb). The command ¡No se haga! means Stop pretending!

examples.text: Gerardo se hace el tonto, pero habla inglés perfectamente.
examples.translation: Gerardo plays dumb, but he speaks English perfectly.

examples.text: Profesor, ¡no se haga! Usted sabe la respuesta.
examples.translation: Professor, don’t pretend! You know the answer.

explanations.title: Convertirse en: to turn into
explanations.body: Convertirse en + noun also means to become, often for a big change: Ella se convirtió en una gran artista. Use ponerse + adjective for a mood or a temporary change: Me puse nervioso (I got nervous).

exercises.prompt: Mauricio se ___ abogado después de muchos años de estudio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mauricio became a lawyer after many years of study.

exercises.prompt: Mis primos se ___ médicos en México.
exercises.promptTranslation: My cousins became doctors in Mexico.

exercises.prompt: Yo me ___ rico gracias a mi trabajo.
exercises.promptTranslation: I became rich thanks to my work.

exercises.prompt: Ella se ___ en una gran artista.
exercises.promptTranslation: She became a great artist.

exercises.prompt: Gerardo se hace el ___, pero habla inglés muy bien.
exercises.explanation: Hacerse el tonto = to play dumb.
exercises.promptTranslation: Gerardo plays dumb, but he speaks English very well.

exercises.prompt: Profesor, ¡no se ___! Usted sabe la respuesta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Professor, don’t pretend! You know the answer.

exercises.prompt: Which verb do you use for a mood, as in “I got nervous”?
exercises.explanation: Me puse nervioso = I got nervous.

exercises.prompt: What does “Maricela se hizo rica” mean?
What does “Se hace el tonto” mean?
exercises.explanation: Hacerse el tonto = to pretend not to know.

lessons.title: 238. Words for an accident
lessons.subtitle: El autobús chocó, rodó y cayó. Hubo varios heridos.

explanations.title: Vocabulary: the road
explanations.body: These words appear in news about road accidents. Chocar means to crash; it is followed by con or contra. Rodar is to roll and caer is to fall.

explanations.title: People and injuries
explanations.body: Words for people and their condition: el herido (injured person), el muerto (dead person), el peregrino (pilgrim, traveler on a religious journey), el pasajero (passenger). Say de gravedad for seriously: un herido de gravedad.

examples.text: El conductor perdió el control en una curva peligrosa.
examples.translation: The driver lost control on a dangerous curve.

examples.text: El autobús chocó con un camión.
examples.translation: The bus crashed into a truck.

examples.text: El autobús rodó hacia un barranco y cayó.
examples.translation: The bus rolled toward a ravine and fell.

examples.text: Hubo un herido de gravedad.
examples.translation: There was one seriously injured person.

explanations.title: The verbs in the preterite
explanations.body: Chocar changes c to qu in the yo form (choqué). Caer has a y-change: cayó, cayeron, because the i would fall between two vowels. Rodar is regular: rodó, rodaron.

exercises.promptTranslation: The bus crashed into a truck.

lessons.title: 239. A bus accident in the news
lessons.subtitle: Un autobús salió de la carretera cerca de las once y media de la noche.

explanations.title: Read the news report
explanations.body: News reports tell what happened (preterite) in order. Read this short report and find who, what, when and where.

examples.text: Un autobús con cuarenta y un peregrinos salió de la carretera el miércoles, cerca de las once y media de la noche.
examples.translation: A bus with forty-one pilgrims left the highway on Wednesday, near eleven thirty at night.

examples.text: El conductor perdió el control en una curva peligrosa.
examples.translation: The driver lost control on a dangerous curve.

examples.text: El autobús chocó, rodó hacia un barranco y cayó quince metros.

examples.translation: One passenger died and forty were injured; one of them seriously.

examples.text: Los equipos de rescate llevaron a los heridos al centro de salud.
examples.translation: The rescue teams took the injured to the health center.

explanations.title: How a news report is built
explanations.body: A report usually starts with the main event, then gives the place and the time, and ends with the people affected and what happened next. The verbs are in the preterite.

rows: Un autobús salió de la carretera.
En una curva de la carretera.

exercises.promptTranslation: The rescue teams took the injured to the health center.

lessons.title: 240. Resultar + adjective: how people ended up
lessons.subtitle: Dos personas resultaron heridas. Nadie resultó herido.

explanations.title: Resultar: to end up, to turn out
explanations.body: News reports often use resultar + adjective to say how people ended up after an event, usually something bad. The adjective agrees with the people: herido, herida, heridos, heridas.

examples.text: Dos personas resultaron heridas en el accidente.
examples.translation: Two people were injured in the accident.

examples.text: Un conductor resultó herido de gravedad.

explanations.title: Adjectives often used with resultar
explanations.body: Learn this list. Remember that these adjectives change their ending to match who or what they describe.

explanations.title: A set pattern
explanations.body: Use the preterite of resultar (resultó, resultaron) in the news. In everyday talk you can use estar or quedar instead: Quedó herido, Está herido.

lessons.title: 241. Headlines and the five questions
lessons.subtitle: ¿Quién? ¿Qué? ¿Cuándo? ¿Dónde? ¿Por qué?

explanations.title: The five questions of a news story
explanations.body: Journalists answer five questions in the first lines of a story. Use them to pull out the key facts.

explanations.title: A short news item
explanations.body: Read this report and find the five answers.

examples.text: Un incendio destruyó una fábrica de muebles en las afueras de Lima el domingo por la tarde.

explanations.title: Headlines are short
explanations.body: A headline gives the main fact in few words. It often leaves out the article and may use the present tense for a past event: Incendio destruye fábrica en Lima. Según + a person or group tells where the information came from.

examples.text: Incendio destruye fábrica de muebles en Lima

lessons.title: 242. Ancient cultures of the Americas: words
lessons.subtitle: los mayas, los aztecas, los incas, los olmecas

explanations.title: Four great cultures
explanations.body: Four great pre-Columbian cultures appear in this unit. Pre-Columbian means before Columbus arrived in 1492. The names of the peoples are masculine plural: los mayas, los aztecas, los incas, los olmecas.

explanations.title: Words about ancient societies
explanations.body: Use these words to talk about how a society was organized.

explanations.title: Dates
explanations.body: Dates before Christ use a.C. (antes de Cristo), and dates after use d.C. (después de Cristo). Centuries are read with ordinal or cardinal numbers: el siglo catorce.

examples.text: Los olmecas vivieron en México mucho antes que los aztecas.
examples.translation: The Olmecs lived in Mexico long before the Aztecs.

examples.translation: The Incas built their capital in the mountains.

lessons.title: 245. Crime in the news: a street robbery

explanations.title: Vocabulary: crime news
explanations.body: Crime reports use a fixed set of words. The person who does the crime is el agresor (attacker) or el ladrón (thief). The person who suffers it is la víctima, even when the person is a man. Los testigos are the witnesses.

explanations.title: A street robbery, as reported
explanations.body: Read this report. Every verb is in the preterite because each action finished. Find who, what, when and where.

explanations.title: Spanish uses a for people

lessons.title: 246. The imperfect: what was happening?
lessons.subtitle: Luis caminaba a la universidad. Llovía y hacía frío.

explanations.title: Two past tenses
explanations.body: Spanish has two simple past tenses. The preterite tells what happened: events that began or ended, one after another. The imperfect tells what was happening or what used to happen: habits, ongoing actions, descriptions, states, time and age. They are not interchangeable.

rows: Mi abuela cocinó una sopa ayer.
Mi abuela cocinaba todos los domingos.

explanations.title: What the imperfect does
explanations.body: Use the imperfect for: 1) habits and repeated actions (I used to…); 2) ongoing actions with no stated beginning or end (was/were -ing); 3) descriptions; 4) states of being, such as moods and health; 5) the time of day; 6) age.

rows: Mi abuela cocinaba todos los domingos.
My grandmother used to cook every Sunday.
Los niños jugaban en el parque.
The children were playing in the park.
Hacía sol y el mar estaba tranquilo.
It was sunny and the sea was calm.
Eran las ocho de la noche.
My brother was ten years old.

explanations.title: Words that go with the imperfect
explanations.body: These words often signal the imperfect: siempre, todos los días, todos los veranos, cada año, frecuentemente, generalmente, a menudo, antes (before, in the past), en aquella época (in those days), mientras (while). Solía + infinitive also means used to.

examples.text: Todos los veranos íbamos a la playa.

lessons.title: 247. Imperfect of -ar verbs

explanations.title: The -ar endings
explanations.body: Drop -ar and add -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban. Only the nosotros form has a written accent. There are no stem changes, even in verbs like jugar or pensar: jugaba, pensaba.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice that yo and él / ella have the same form. The context or the subject tells you who it is.

lessons.title: 248. Imperfect of -er and -ir verbs

explanations.title: One set of endings for -er and -ir
explanations.body: Drop -er or -ir and add -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Every form has an accent on the í, so yo and él / ella are identical: comía.

explanations.title: Irregular verbs are regular here
explanations.body: Verbs that are irregular in the present or the preterite are regular in the imperfect: tener → tenía, hacer → hacía, poder → podía, decir → decía, dormir → dormía, pedir → pedía, salir → salía, venir → venía. The only irregular verbs in the imperfect are ir, ser and ver.

lessons.title: 249. Imperfect of ir, ser and ver
lessons.subtitle: iba, íbamos · era, éramos · veía, veíamos

explanations.title: The three irregular verbs
explanations.body: Ir, ser and ver are the only irregular verbs in the imperfect. Ir takes -ba endings after an i- stem; ser has the stem er-; ver keeps the e of its stem: ve- + -ía = veía.

explanations.title: In use
explanations.body: Use iba for places you used to go to, era for descriptions and identity, and veía for what you used to see or watch.

explanations.body: Use antes (before) and ahora (now) to contrast. The imperfect talks about the past; the present talks about today.

lessons.title: 251. Describing the past: weather, places and people
lessons.subtitle: Era alto y delgado. Llovía y la calle estaba vacía.

explanations.title: Scenery and weather
explanations.body: Use the imperfect to paint the scene before the action. Weather expressions: hacía frío, hacía calor, hacía viento, hacía sol, llovía (it was raining), nevaba (it was snowing), había niebla (it was foggy).

Había mucha gente en la plaza.

explanations.title: People: appearance and clothes
explanations.body: Describe how people looked with ser (era alto, tenía el pelo negro) and what they were wearing with llevaba or vestía. Use estaba for how they felt.

lessons.title: 252. Time and age in the past

explanations.title: What time was it?
explanations.body: To give the time in the past, use era for one o'clock (era la una) and eran for all other hours. The time is given in the imperfect, even when the main action of the story is in the preterite.

explanations.title: Time + action
explanations.body: Combine the time in the imperfect with a preterite action using cuando: Eran las siete cuando llegó el tren. The time sets the scene and the preterite gives the event.

explanations.title: How old were you?
explanations.body: Age in the past uses tener in the imperfect: tenía veinte años. With a time, use cuando tenía + number + años (when I was … years old). Use the preterite for the exact moment of an event, not the age.

lessons.title: 254. How the Inca empire worked
lessons.subtitle: Los incas se organizaban en comunidades llamadas ayllus.

explanations.title: Habits of a vanished society
explanations.body: When we describe how a society worked in the past, we use the imperfect: what its people used to do, how things used to be. The Incas lived in the Andes. Their capital was Cusco.

examples.text: El imperio inca se organizaba en comunidades llamadas ayllus.

explanations.title: Roads and quipus
explanations.body: The emperor kept control through a network of roads that connected every region with Cusco. Along the road there were rest stations called tambos. The Incas had no writing, but they used the quipus, knotted strings, to record numbers and messages.

explanations.title: Describing a person for the police
explanations.body: A witness describes the scene and the person with the imperfect: what the street was like, how the person looked, what he was wearing. The event itself is told in the preterite.

lessons.title: 256. The gerund: forms to know
lessons.subtitle: hablando, comiendo, escribiendo, leyendo, durmiendo, pidiendo

explanations.title: Regular gerunds
explanations.body: The gerund (el gerundio, the -ing form) is made from the stem: -ar verbs take -ando and -er / -ir verbs take -iendo. The gerund never changes for gender or number.

explanations.title: Gerunds with a spelling or stem change
explanations.body: Verbs with a vowel before -er / -ir change i to y: leer → leyendo, caer → cayendo, traer → trayendo, oír → oyendo, construir → construyendo, huir → huyendo. Stem-changing -ir verbs also change in the gerund: dormir → durmiendo, morir → muriendo, pedir → pidiendo, decir → diciendo, seguir → siguiendo, venir → viniendo, vestirse → vistiéndose, divertirse → divirtiéndose.

explanations.title: Pronouns and the gerund
explanations.body: A pronoun can attach to the gerund (with an accent to keep the stress) or go before estar: Está vistiéndose / Se está vistiendo. The gerund is also used with estar, seguir, andar and pasar.

explanations.title: Estaba + gerund
explanations.body: To stress an action in progress in the past, use estaba, estabas, estaba, estábamos, estaban + the gerund. It usually gets interrupted by a preterite event, introduced by cuando.

explanations.title: Interrupted actions
explanations.body: The progressive is the background and the preterite is the interruption. Other tenses of estar also work: Estuvo estudiando toda la noche means he spent the whole night studying (a finished stretch of time).

explanations.title: Keep on doing something
explanations.body: Seguir + gerund and continuar + gerund both mean to keep on doing something. They can be used in any tense. Seguir has a stem change (sigo, sigue) and in the preterite the third person is siguió, siguieron.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Continuar means exactly the same: continuó corriendo, continuaban estudiando. The gerund is always in the invariable -ando / -iendo form.

explanations.title: Pasar + time + gerund
explanations.body: Pasar + a period of time + gerund means to spend time doing something. It is used in all tenses.

explanations.body: Andar + gerund is informal. It says that someone is going around doing something, often without a clear purpose. ¿Qué andas haciendo? means What are you up to?

explanations.body: Llevar + a period of time + gerund tells how long you have been doing something: Llevo tres años estudiando español (I have been studying Spanish for three years).

lessons.title: 262. Review: the imperfect and the progressive

explanations.title: Imperfect forms at a glance
explanations.body: Regular -ar verbs: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -aban. Regular -er / -ir verbs: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían. Only ir, ser and ver are irregular.

explanations.title: The progressive
explanations.body: Past progressive = estaba / estabas / estaba / estábamos / estaban + gerund. With seguir, pasar and andar, the gerund tells how an action continues, how time is spent, or what someone is up to.

lessons.title: 264. Repeated or completed? Imperfect versus preterite

explanations.title: Habit or single event
explanations.body: Use the imperfect for habits and repeated actions in the past, and the preterite for a completed action at a definite moment. The same verb can appear in both tenses with different meanings.

explanations.title: Signal words
explanations.body: Words that signal repetition point to the imperfect: siempre, todos los días, cada verano, frecuentemente, generalmente, antes. Words that point to one moment signal the preterite: ayer, anoche, el lunes, una vez, el año pasado, hace tres meses.

explanations.title: No beginning or end, or both stated
explanations.body: The imperfect looks at an action in the middle, with no start or end stated. The preterite is used when the beginning, the end or the length of the action is stated.

explanations.title: Starting and stopping
explanations.body: Verbs for starting and stopping, such as empezar, comenzar, terminar and renunciar, are normally used in the preterite because they name the edge of an action. Durante + a period and por + a period also point to the preterite.

lessons.title: 266. Setting the scene, then the action
lessons.subtitle: Aunque hacía viento y llovía, salí a caminar.

explanations.title: Background and plot
explanations.body: In a story, the imperfect paints the scene and the conditions, while the preterite moves the plot forward. Think of a film: the set is the imperfect and the action is the preterite.

rows: …salí a caminar para conocer la ciudad.
Había mucha gente en la plaza…

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: Notice that the same sentence often has both tenses. The scene verbs are hacía, llovía, estaban, había, era. The action verbs are salí, abrí, busqué, entramos.

lessons.title: 267. Interrupted actions and simultaneous actions

explanations.title: Imperfect + cuando + preterite
explanations.body: The imperfect says what was going on, and the preterite says what interrupted it. Cuando and de repente often introduce the interruption.

explanations.title: Two actions at the same time
explanations.body: Mientras links two actions that happen at the same time. Both verbs are in the imperfect. When two completed actions follow one another, use two preterites: Cuando llegué, ella salió.

lessons.title: 268. Hubo or había?
lessons.subtitle: Hubo un accidente. Había mucha gente en el estadio.

explanations.title: Two forms of haber in the past
explanations.body: Hubo and había both mean there was or there were. Use hubo when you answer ¿Qué pasó? (an event). Use había when you describe the scene or the conditions. Neither changes for plural nouns.

rows: Había mucha gente en el estadio.
Hubo tres muertos y dos heridos.
Hubo un problema con el vuelo.

explanations.title: How to choose
explanations.body: Ask yourself: is it an event that happened, or something that was just there? Counting victims or reporting an incident uses hubo. Describing the room, the weather or the crowd uses había.

lessons.title: 269. Verbs that mostly describe: estar, ser, tener, llevar, llamarse

explanations.title: Usually imperfect
explanations.body: Some verbs mostly describe, so they are usually in the imperfect: estar, ser, tener, llevar (to wear), llamarse, and others like lucir, brillar, poseer and ubicarse (to be located).

explanations.title: When the preterite is possible
explanations.body: These verbs take the preterite when a limit is stated or when the meaning changes into an event. Estuve en Lima tres días. Tuve miedo de repente means I got scared. Fue un día largo summarizes the whole day.

lessons.title: 270. Which tense? A checklist
lessons.subtitle: ¿Evento o fondo? Pretérito o imperfecto.

explanations.title: Two questions before you choose
explanations.body: Ask: 1) Is this an event that moved the story forward, with a clear beginning, ending or moment? Use the preterite. 2) Is it a background, a habit, a description, a time, an age or an action in progress? Use the imperfect.

explanations.title: A mini-story with both
explanations.body: In this short story, the imperfect gives the background and the preterite gives the events. Underline the events and circle the background.

examples.text: Era sábado y hacía sol. Mi hermano y yo íbamos al parque.

explanations.title: Common signals
explanations.body: Pretérito: ayer, anoche, el año pasado, de repente, en ese momento, una vez, primero, luego, por fin. Imperfecto: siempre, antes, todos los días, mientras, cada año, en aquella época, a veces.

explanations.title: Read the story
explanations.body: Read this first-person account. The imperfect gives the scene and what people were doing. The preterite gives the sudden events.

explanations.title: A crime story with both tenses
explanations.body: Crime news mixes the two tenses. The imperfect gives the circumstances (what was happening, what the people looked like). The preterite tells the events in order. Read this account.

explanations.body: Amenazar changes z to c in the yo form (amenacé). Perseguir changes e to i in the third person of the preterite: persiguió, persiguieron. Detener is irregular: detuvo, detuvieron.

explanations.body: The police use both tenses when they question a witness: the imperfect for where you were and what you were doing, the preterite for what you saw and what happened. They address the witness as usted.

explanations.body: Notice how the answers keep the same tense as the question: the imperfect with what was going on, the preterite with events.

lessons.title: 275. Crime vocabulary: people and crimes
lessons.subtitle: el delincuente, el culpable, el sospechoso, el delito, el robo

explanations.title: The people in a crime story
explanations.body: News stories use precise words for the people involved. El delincuente is a general word for a criminal. El ladrón is a thief, el asaltante is a robber who attacks, el homicida is a killer, el culpable is the guilty person, el sospechoso is the suspect, la víctima is the victim, and el testigo is the witness.

explanations.title: The crimes
explanations.body: The crime itself is el delito (general), el crimen (serious), el robo (theft), el asalto (hold-up), el asesinato or el homicidio (murder), el secuestro (kidnapping), la extorsión (extortion), el fraude (fraud), and la estafa (scam). Most end in -o, -ción or -e.

explanations.title: Gender reminder
explanations.body: La víctima has fixed feminine gender: it is feminine even when the victim is a man. El testigo, like el delincuente and el culpable, changes only the article: el / la testigo, el / la delincuente, el / la culpable.

lessons.title: 276. The police and the courts

explanations.title: From arrest to trial
explanations.body: A criminal case follows a sequence, and each step has its verb. The police detener or arrestar the suspect and investigar the crime. The prosecutor acusar. The judge (el juez) decides in a trial (el juicio). The sentence is la condena and the verb is condenar.

explanations.title: Prison words
explanations.body: La cárcel (or la prisión) is the prison. La celda is the cell. Estar tras las rejas means to be behind bars. La fuga is an escape and fugarse is to escape. Cumplir una condena means to serve a sentence.

explanations.title: A case in the preterite
explanations.body: Reporting the stages of a case uses the preterite.

lessons.title: 277. Kidnapping and missing persons
lessons.subtitle: El secuestrador pidió un rescate. La policía busca al desaparecido.

explanations.title: Kidnapping words
explanations.body: El secuestro is kidnapping, el secuestrador is the kidnapper, and el rehén is the hostage. Be careful: el rescate means both the ransom (money asked for) and the rescue. Context tells you which. Liberar is to release or free.

explanations.title: Missing persons
explanations.body: Un desaparecido is a person who has disappeared. El paradero is the whereabouts: se desconoce su paradero means his whereabouts are unknown. La recompensa is the reward offered for information.

lessons.title: 278. Attacks and explosions in the news

explanations.title: Vocabulary: attacks
explanations.body: Reports on attacks use a stable vocabulary. El atentado is the attack (a deliberate violent act against people or places). El ataque is the broader word. La explosión or el estallido is an explosion, and explotar or estallar is to explode. La bomba is the bomb, and el coche bomba is a car bomb.

explanations.title: How a report sounds
explanations.body: These reports use the preterite for what happened and often finish with the toll (el saldo) and the state of the investigation in the present.

examples.translation: The authorities are investigating who placed the bomb.

lessons.title: 279. Kinds of weapons: the vocabulary

explanations.title: Categories
explanations.body: News reports and police documents classify weapons into categories. Arma is feminine but takes el in the singular: el arma, las armas. Armas de fuego are firearms. Armas blancas are bladed weapons: knives, machetes. Armas cortas are handguns. Armas largas are rifles and shotguns. Armas de guerra are military weapons.

explanations.title: Related words
explanations.body: Municiones are ammunition and un disparo is a shot. Disparar is to shoot. A bullet can be una bala or un proyectil. You may also see armas de uso civil and armas de uso exclusivo del ejército in laws.

explanations.title: Read the report

explanations.title: A police raid
explanations.body: In a raid (el allanamiento), the police enter a house with an order from a judge. Incautar means to seize (take as evidence). The things seized are described with the passive or active voice. This report is original, written to practice the vocabulary.

lessons.title: 282. Translating news headlines

explanations.title: How headlines work
explanations.body: Headlines save space. They usually drop articles, use the present for past events (Detienen a un sospechoso = They arrested a suspect), and use deja or dejó + a number to give a toll: Choque deja dos muertos.

explanations.title: Reading tips
explanations.body: A plural verb without a subject (Detienen, Hallan, Liberan) means someone unspecified did it, usually the police or authorities: translate it as a passive: A suspect is arrested. Dos puntos (:) split the headline into topic and detail.

lessons.title: 283. Tirar: a verb with many uses

explanations.title: The basic meanings
explanations.body: Tirar has three main meanings: to throw, to shoot or fire (in the expression tirar un balazo), and to pull (tirar de + noun). In everyday talk it has many other uses.

rows: Los niños tiraron piedras al río.
The children threw stones into the river.
Los estudiantes tiran de la puerta para entrar.
The students pull the door to get in.
I threw away the old food.

explanations.title: Idioms with tirar
explanations.body: Four idioms are very common in speech: tirar algo por la borda (to waste something), tirar una moneda al aire (to flip a coin), tirar la casa por la ventana (to spare no expense) and tirar la toalla (to throw in the towel, to give up).

explanations.title: Forming the past participle
explanations.body: The past participle is the form that works like an adjective (“detained”, “lost”). Drop the infinitive ending and add -ado to -ar verbs, or -ido to -er and -ir verbs.

lessons.title: 288. The passive voice with ser

explanations.title: Subject receives the action
explanations.body: In the active voice the subject does the action: La policía detuvo al ladrón. In the passive voice the subject receives it: El ladrón fue detenido. The passive is built with ser + past participle, and the participle agrees with the subject. It is typical of newspapers (estilo periodístico) and much rarer in everyday speech.

explanations.title: Most often in the preterite
explanations.body: Any tense of ser can be used, but the news most often reports finished events, so fue / fueron + participle is the pattern you will meet again and again.

lessons.title: 290. Three ways to say it: active, passive, and se

explanations.title: Active, ser-passive, se-passive
explanations.body: The same event can be told three ways. Active: the doer is the subject. Ser-passive: written, formal, often names the agent with por. Se-passive: very common in speech and in news when nobody needs to be named; the verb agrees with the thing (se encontró el arma, se encontraron las armas).

explanations.title: Which to use
explanations.body: In conversation, choose the active voice or the se form. Keep ser + participle for reading and writing the news. Avoid combining se with por: if you name the agent, use ser.

lessons.title: 292. Por (1): exchange, means, movement through
lessons.subtitle: La familia pagó mucho dinero por la liberación del niño.

explanations.title: Three uses of por
explanations.body: Por looks backward at what pushes or fills an action. Use it for (1) an exchange (paying for something), (2) the means or manner by which something is done, and (3) movement through or along a place.

rows: La familia pagó mucho dinero {por} la liberación del niño.
The family paid a lot of money for the release of the child.
They spoke with him by phone.
The criminal escaped along the river.
Caminamos {por} el centro de la ciudad.
We walked through the center of the city.

lessons.title: 293. Por (2): cause, agent, length of time, set phrases
lessons.subtitle: Un hombre murió por la explosión de una bomba.

explanations.title: More uses of por
explanations.body: Por also gives the cause (because of), the agent in the passive (by), and how long something lasts (for).

A man died because of a bomb explosion.
El puente fue construido {por} los españoles.
The bridge was built by the Spaniards.

explanations.body: Many everyday expressions use por. Learn them as chunks.

lessons.title: 294. Para: recipient, purpose, destination, deadline, employer

explanations.title: Five uses of para
explanations.body: Para looks forward, toward a goal. Use it for (1) the person something is intended for, (2) purpose (in order to + verb), (3) destination, (4) a deadline, and (5) the employer you work for.

My brother works for the government.

lessons.title: 295. Por or para? Pairs that change meaning

explanations.title: One word changes the whole idea
explanations.body: Often only the preposition tells the listener what you mean. Por points to the cause, the exchange, the route or the duration. Para points to the goal, the recipient, the destination or the deadline.

explanations.title: Quick map
explanations.body: Participle as adjective: agrees with the noun (la puerta abierta). Estar + participle: a result (la puerta está abierta). Ser + participle: the passive (la puerta fue abierta por un vecino). Se: no agent (se abrió la puerta).

lessons.title: 310. Cuyo: whose

explanations.title: Cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas
explanations.body: Cuyo means “whose”. It links a person or thing to something that belongs to them. Unlike English, cuyo agrees in gender and number with what is possessed (the noun that comes right after it), not with the owner.

examples.translation: The women whose ideas changed history were brave.

explanations.title: Same verb, different meaning
explanations.body: Some verbs change their meaning depending on whether you use the imperfect or the preterite. The imperfect describes a state that was already going on; the preterite marks a single moment that started something.

examples.translation: I knew that Carlos was going out with her.

examples.translation: Yesterday I found out that Carlos is going out with her.

exercises.promptTranslation: I met Marta at a party.

explanations.title: Poder and querer
explanations.body: In the preterite, poder means that you managed to do it. No poder means you tried and failed. Querer means you tried, and no querer means you refused.

lessons.title: 314. Tener que and ir a: had to, was going to
lessons.subtitle: Tenía que hacer la tarea, pero no la terminé.

explanations.title: Tener que and ir a
explanations.body: With tener que, the imperfect only says you were supposed to; the preterite says you had to and you did it. With ir a, the imperfect is “was going to” (it may not have happened) and the preterite is “went to”.

rows: I was supposed to do it.
I had to, and I did.

examples.translation: I was supposed to do my homework, but I did not finish it.

examples.translation: I had to do my homework and I finished it.

examples.text: Iba a correr, pero me enfermé.
examples.translation: I was going to run, but I got sick.

examples.text: Fui a correr por dos horas.
examples.translation: I went running for two hours.

explanations.title: All eight at a glance
explanations.body: Keep this summary: the preterite tends to point to a decision or result, the imperfect to the state of mind.

explanations.title: Tanto as an adjective
explanations.body: Before a noun, tanto means “so much” or “so many” and agrees with the noun in gender and number.

rows: No bebas tanto café por la noche.
Don't drink so much coffee at night.
Hay tanta gente en la plaza.
There are so many people in the square.
Why do you have so many books?
She used to take so many medicines.

explanations.title: Tanto and tan as adverbs
explanations.body: As an adverb, tanto does not change: no trabajes tanto. Before an adjective or another adverb it shortens to tan: es tan simpático.

examples.translation: Don't work so much.

examples.text: Él es tan simpático.
examples.translation: He is so nice.

examples.text: Llegaste tan tarde.
examples.translation: You arrived so late.

explanations.title: As much as, as many as, as … as
explanations.body: Use tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + como to say “as much / as many … as”. Use tan + adjective or adverb + como to say “as … as”. After a verb, use tanto como.

Juan used to drink as much coffee as Rosa.

My brother is as tall as my father.

lessons.title: 319. Bueno, malo, mejor, peor

explanations.title: Good and bad
explanations.body: Bueno and malo are adjectives: they agree with the noun and usually go before it. Before a masculine singular noun they lose the final -o: un buen amigo, un mal amigo.

explanations.title: Better and worse
explanations.body: Mejor (better) and peor (worse) serve both as adjectives and as adverbs. The adjectives add -es in the plural; the adverbs never change. The comparison uses que.

explanations.title: More than, less than
explanations.body: Más … que and menos … que compare two things. Mejor … que and peor … que usually replace más bueno and más malo. Before a number, use de instead of que.

This book is more interesting than the other.

Su sueldo era mejor que el mío.
His salary was better than mine.
There were more than ten people.

lessons.title: 321. Superlatives: the most, the best
lessons.subtitle: Esta es la ciudad más grande del país.

explanations.title: The most … of
explanations.body: To say “the most …” use the definite article + más (or menos) + adjective. After the superlative, “of” or “in” is usually de (del mundo, del país). For “the best” and “the worst” use el / la mejor and el / la peor.

rows: el / la / los / las + más + adj + de
Esta es la ciudad más grande del país.
This is the biggest city in the country.
el / la + noun + más + adj + de
Es el héroe más famoso de todos.
He is the most famous hero of all.
el / la / los / las + mejor(es) + de
Ella es la mejor de todas.
She is the best of all.
Fue el peor día de mi vida.
It was the worst day of my life.

examples.translation: It is one of the most beautiful cities in the world.

lessons.title: 322. Lo más, lo mejor, lo peor

explanations.title: Lo + superlative for ideas
explanations.body: To talk about an idea or situation rather than a specific noun, use the neuter article lo: lo más difícil, lo mejor, lo peor. Lo que means “what” or “that which”.

rows: Lo más difícil fue hablar con él.
The most difficult thing was talking to him.
Lo mejor es que me escuchó.
The best part is that he listened to me.
Lo peor es que no dijo la verdad.
The worst part is that he did not tell the truth.

lessons.title: 323. The absolute superlative: -ísimo

explanations.title: Extremely …
explanations.body: To say “extremely” or “incredibly”, drop the final vowel of the adjective (if it has one) and add -ísimo, -ísima, -ísimos or -ísimas. The ending still agrees with the noun.

explanations.title: Spelling changes
explanations.body: To keep the same sound, some adjectives change spelling before -ísimo: c → qu, g → gu, z → c.

lessons.title: 325. The historical present
lessons.subtitle: Colón llega a América en mil cuatrocientos noventa y dos.

explanations.title: Telling the past in the present
explanations.body: Spanish writers often narrate historical events in the present tense (el presente histórico). It makes the event feel close to the reader. It appears in encyclopedias, textbooks and the news.

rows: Colón llegó a América en mil cuatrocientos noventa y dos.
Colón llega a América en mil cuatrocientos noventa y dos.
Hidalgo llamó al pueblo en mil ochocientos diez.
Hidalgo llama al pueblo en mil ochocientos diez.
Perón ganó las elecciones en mil novecientos cuarenta y seis.
Perón gana las elecciones en mil novecientos cuarenta y seis.

explanations.title: A date or a reference to the past is needed
explanations.body: Use the historical present only when the sentence has a clear reference to the past, usually a year. Without it, the reader cannot tell whether you mean now or then, so use the preterite.

examples.text: En el año doscientos dieciocho antes de Cristo, los romanos llegan a España.
examples.translation: In 218 BC the Romans arrive in Spain.

lessons.title: 332. The accidental se: it slipped out of my hands
lessons.subtitle: Se me olvidó la llave.

explanations.title: Things happen to you
explanations.body: Spanish often describes accidents and slips as if they happened to you, not as if you did them. Instead of “I forgot the key” you can say “the key was forgotten on me”: Se me olvidó la llave. The person is shown by an indirect object pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les), and the thing is the subject.

rows: A mí se me olvidó la llave.
A ti se te cayeron los libros.
A Lupe se le derramó la sopa.
A nosotros se nos acabó la gasolina.
A los niños se les perdieron los zapatos.

explanations.title: The verb agrees with the thing
explanations.body: Just as with gustar, the thing that is lost, broken or forgotten is the subject, so the verb is singular or plural to match it. Possessive adjectives are not needed: the pronoun already shows whose it is.

explanations.title: Who is it? Add a + person
explanations.body: Se le and se les can refer to many people (él, ella, usted, ellos, ustedes). To make it clear who you mean, start with a + the person.

explanations.body: The ordinary sentence names you as the doer: Rompí el vaso. The accidental se removes the blame: Se me rompió el vaso. Use the second when something happened by accident or when you do not want to sound responsible.

I burned dinner. / Dinner got burned.

lessons.title: 338. Review: the imperfect and the preterite together
lessons.subtitle: Eran las cinco y yo leía cuando sonó el teléfono.

explanations.title: The imperfect: the scene
explanations.body: Use the imperfect for the stage on which the story happens: description, habits, actions in progress, feelings and health, the time and a person's age.

rows: La casa era vieja y tenía ventanas grandes.
The house was old and had big windows.
Cada verano íbamos a la playa.
Every summer we used to go to the beach.
Yo leía cuando sonó el teléfono.
I was reading when the phone rang.
Estaba cansado y me dolía la cabeza.
I was tired and my head hurt.
Eran las cinco y tenía diez años.
It was five o’clock and I was ten years old.

explanations.title: The preterite: the events
explanations.body: Use the preterite for the events themselves: a single action, an interruption, the main event, the beginning or end of something, or an action that lasted a stated period.

rows: Yo leía cuando sonó el teléfono.
I was reading when the phone rang.
Hubo un accidente en la calle.
There was an accident in the street.
Empezó a llover y terminó la fiesta.
It started to rain and the party ended.

lessons.title: 339. A stated period of time calls for the preterite

explanations.title: When the time is named
explanations.body: Even when a sentence describes a state, a feeling or a habit (all imperfect territory), a stated, bounded length of time such as por tres años, durante una semana or todo el día usually makes it a completed block, so the preterite is the normal choice. Habits and background scenes with no bound stay in the imperfect.

explanations.title: Two uses of se
explanations.body: The passive se has a thing as its subject, and the verb agrees with it: Se venden casas. The impersonal se talks about people in general and the verb stays singular: Se vive bien aquí. If the object is a specific person with the personal a, the verb also stays singular: Se busca a los testigos.

rows: Se vive bien en esta ciudad.
One lives well in this city.
One does not work on Sundays.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ casas en esta calle.
exercises.promptTranslation: Houses are for sale on this street.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ bien en esta ciudad.
exercises.promptTranslation: One lives well in this city.

exercises.prompt: No se ___ los domingos.
exercises.promptTranslation: One does not work on Sundays.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ español en México.
exercises.promptTranslation: Spanish is spoken in Mexico.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ a los testigos.
exercises.promptTranslation: The witnesses are being sought.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ platos típicos en este restaurante.
exercises.promptTranslation: Typical dishes are served at this restaurant.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is impersonal?
Why is it “Se detuvo a los ladrones” and not “Se detuvieron a los ladrones”?
options: The personal a keeps the verb singular
exercises.explanation: Standard Spanish: with personal a, no agreement.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a passive se?

lessons.title: 346. Passive se in the news
lessons.subtitle: Se decretó un toque de queda y se cerraron las escuelas.

explanations.title: News reports love the passive se
explanations.body: Reporters often avoid naming the doer, either because it is unknown or because the action matters more. Read these news sentences and identify the thing and the agreeing verb.

examples.text: Se decretó un toque de queda en la ciudad.
examples.translation: A curfew was decreed in the city.

examples.text: Se cerraron las escuelas por el mal tiempo.
examples.translation: The schools were closed because of the bad weather.

examples.text: Se reportaron varios heridos en la carretera.
examples.translation: Several injured people were reported on the highway.

examples.text: Se levantó la medida después de tres días.
examples.translation: The measure was lifted after three days.

examples.text: Se firmó un cese del fuego entre las partes.
examples.translation: A ceasefire was signed between the parties.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ un toque de queda en la ciudad.
exercises.promptTranslation: A curfew was decreed in the city.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ las escuelas por el mal tiempo.
exercises.promptTranslation: The schools were closed because of the bad weather.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ varios heridos en la carretera.
exercises.promptTranslation: Several injured people were reported on the highway.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ la medida después de tres días.
exercises.promptTranslation: The measure was lifted after three days.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ un cese del fuego entre las partes.
exercises.promptTranslation: A ceasefire was signed between the parties.

exercises.prompt: Ayer se ___ las fronteras.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday the borders were closed.

exercises.prompt: What does “Se reportaron varios heridos” mean?
options: They reported several injuries on purpose

exercises.prompt: Why do news reports use the passive se so often?
options: It is shorter than the future
The doer is unknown or unimportant

exercises.prompt: Which noun decides the verb in “Se cerraron las escuelas”?

lessons.title: 347. Retirar and retirarse
lessons.subtitle: Retiro lo dicho: Arnulfo no es tonto.

explanations.title: One verb, several meanings
explanations.body: Retirar without the reflexive pronoun acts on something else (money, an object, words). Retirarse, with the reflexive, is about you leaving or stepping away.

rows: Me voy a retirar ahora; tengo que trabajar mañana.
I am going to leave now; I have to work tomorrow.
El futbolista se retiró muy joven.
The soccer player retired very young.
Señor, tiene que retirarse de ese lugar.
Sir, you have to move away from that place.
Necesito retirar dinero de mi cuenta.
I need to withdraw money from my account.
Retiren las mochilas de la pared.
Move the backpacks away from the wall.
Le retiré la palabra a Pablo.

exercises.prompt: Necesito ___ dinero de mi cuenta.
exercises.explanation: Money is the object → no reflexive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I need to withdraw money from my account.

exercises.prompt: Me voy a ___ ahora.
exercises.explanation: Me is already before voy a, so use the plain infinitive: me voy a retirar.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am going to leave now.

exercises.prompt: Señor, tiene que ___ de ese lugar.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, you have to move away from that place.

exercises.prompt: Retiren las mochilas de la ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: Move the backpacks away from the wall.

exercises.prompt: ___ lo dicho: me equivoqué.
exercises.promptTranslation: I take that back: I was wrong.

exercises.prompt: El futbolista se ___ muy joven.
exercises.promptTranslation: The soccer player retired very young.

exercises.prompt: What does “retirar lo dicho” mean?
options: to take back what you said

exercises.prompt: What does “retirarle la palabra a alguien” mean?
When is retirar not reflexive?
options: when it acts on a thing

lessons.title: 348. Words for wars and revolutions
lessons.subtitle: Un golpe de Estado puede empezar una dictadura.

explanations.title: People, events and places
explanations.body: History reading needs a small, steady set of words. Learn them as families: the event, the people it touches, and the paper that ends it.

explanations.title: Verbs that tell the story
explanations.body: Most of these are regular. Put them in the preterite for events and in the imperfect for the way things were.

examples.text: El dictador gobernó el país durante veinte años.
examples.translation: The dictator governed the country for twenty years.

examples.text: Muchas familias huyeron de la guerra.
examples.translation: Many families fled from the war.

examples.text: Los dos países firmaron un tratado de paz.
examples.translation: The two countries signed a peace treaty.

examples.text: Los campesinos reclamaron sus tierras.
examples.translation: The farmers demanded their land.

examples.text: Los líderes negociaron el cese del fuego.
examples.translation: The leaders negotiated the ceasefire.

explanations.title: A line about civil wars
explanations.body: Here is a sentence about civil wars that you may meet in readings and speeches.

examples.text: No hay guerra más hiriente que entre hermanos y parientes.
examples.translation: There is no war more hurtful than the one between brothers and relatives.

exercises.prompt: Una ___ civil es un conflicto dentro de un país.
exercises.promptTranslation: A civil war is a conflict inside a country.

exercises.prompt: Un ___ de Estado es cuando un grupo quita el poder al gobierno por la fuerza.
exercises.promptTranslation: A coup is when a group takes power from the government by force.

exercises.prompt: Después del golpe, el general estableció una ___ y no hubo elecciones.
exercises.promptTranslation: After the coup, the general set up a dictatorship and there were no elections.

exercises.prompt: Los dos países firmaron un ___ de paz.
exercises.promptTranslation: The two countries signed a peace treaty.

exercises.prompt: Muchos ciudadanos huyeron a otro país como ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many citizens fled to another country as refugees.

exercises.prompt: Los líderes dejaron su país y vivieron en el ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: The leaders left their country and lived in exile.

exercises.prompt: Los campesinos ___ sus tierras.
exercises.promptTranslation: The farmers demanded their land.

exercises.prompt: Which word is always feminine, even when it describes a man?
exercises.explanation: La víctima is feminine for everyone.

exercises.prompt: What does the sentence say?

lessons.title: 349. Reading: the Spanish Civil War
lessons.subtitle: La guerra duró casi tres años.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: Read the story once for the main events. Notice that events use the preterite and the background uses the imperfect.

examples.text: En julio de mil novecientos treinta y seis, un grupo de generales se rebeló contra el gobierno de España.
examples.translation: In July 1936, a group of generals rose up against the government of Spain.

examples.text: Así empezó una guerra civil que duró casi tres años.
examples.translation: That is how a civil war began that lasted almost three years.

examples.text: Murieron muchas personas y muchas familias perdieron su casa.
examples.translation: Many people died and many families lost their homes.

examples.text: Al terminar la guerra, Francisco Franco gobernó el país como dictador hasta su muerte.
examples.translation: When the war ended, Francisco Franco governed the country as a dictator until his death.

examples.text: Miles de personas huyeron a Francia y a México.
examples.translation: Thousands of people fled to France and to Mexico.

examples.text: En mil novecientos treinta y siete, Pablo Picasso pintó el Guernica para recordar a las víctimas de un bombardeo.
examples.translation: In 1937, Pablo Picasso painted Guernica to remember the victims of a bombing.

exercises.prompt: En julio de mil novecientos treinta y seis, un grupo de generales se ___ contra el gobierno.
exercises.promptTranslation: In July 1936, a group of generals rose up against the government.

exercises.prompt: La guerra ___ casi tres años.
exercises.explanation: Stated length of a finished event → preterite.
exercises.promptTranslation: The war lasted almost three years.

exercises.prompt: Franco ___ el país hasta su muerte.
exercises.promptTranslation: Franco governed the country until his death.

exercises.prompt: Al terminar la guerra, miles de personas ___ a Francia.
exercises.explanation: Miles de personas is plural; past event.
exercises.promptTranslation: When the war ended, thousands of people fled to France.

exercises.prompt: Antes de la guerra, mucha gente ___ en el campo.
exercises.promptTranslation: Before the war, many people lived in the countryside.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos treinta y siete, Picasso ___ el Guernica y lo mostró en París.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1937, Picasso painted Guernica and showed it in Paris.

exercises.prompt: How long did the war last?
Where did thousands of Spaniards flee?
Who governed Spain after the war?

lessons.title: 350. Reading: the Cuban Revolution
lessons.subtitle: Batista salió del país el primero de enero.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: The dates here use the ordinal primero for the first of the month. Notice the pattern: el primero de enero, but el dos de enero.

examples.text: En mil novecientos cincuenta y dos, Fulgencio Batista tomó el poder con un golpe de Estado.
examples.translation: In 1952, Fulgencio Batista took power with a coup.

examples.text: Fidel Castro y otros jóvenes criticaron al dictador y organizaron un movimiento.
examples.translation: Fidel Castro and other young people criticized the dictator and organized a movement.

examples.text: Durante varios años, los rebeldes lucharon en las montañas y en las ciudades.
examples.translation: For several years, the rebels fought in the mountains and in the cities.

examples.text: El primero de enero de mil novecientos cincuenta y nueve, Batista salió del país.
examples.translation: On January 1, 1959, Batista left the country.

examples.text: Después, el nuevo gobierno hizo una reforma agraria y cambió las escuelas y los hospitales.
examples.translation: Afterward, the new government carried out a land reform and changed the schools and hospitals.

examples.text: Muchos cubanos se quedaron, pero muchos otros se fueron al exilio.
examples.translation: Many Cubans stayed, but many others went into exile.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos cincuenta y dos, Batista ___ el poder con un golpe de Estado.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1952, Batista took power with a coup.

exercises.prompt: Fidel Castro y otros jóvenes ___ al dictador.
exercises.promptTranslation: Fidel Castro and other young people criticized the dictator.

exercises.prompt: Durante varios años, los rebeldes ___ en las montañas.
exercises.promptTranslation: For several years, the rebels fought in the mountains.

exercises.promptTranslation: On January 1, 1959, Batista left the country.
