exercises.promptTranslation: After the revolution, the new government carried out a land reform.

exercises.prompt: Después de la revolución, muchos cubanos se ___ al exilio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many Cubans went into exile.

exercises.prompt: El ___ de enero fue el primer día del año nuevo.
exercises.explanation: The first of the month: el primero.
exercises.promptTranslation: The first of January was the first day of the new year.

exercises.prompt: Who took power in 1952?
What happened on January 1, 1959?
exercises.explanation: El primero de enero salió del país.

lessons.title: 351. Reading: Guatemala's war and the peace accords
lessons.subtitle: En mil novecientos noventa y seis se firmó la paz.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: This is a harder story, told factually. Notice the quantity doscientas mil: the feminine hundreds agree with personas.

examples.text: La guerra civil de Guatemala empezó en mil novecientos sesenta y terminó en mil novecientos noventa y seis.
examples.translation: Guatemala's civil war began in 1960 and ended in 1996.

examples.text: Fue una guerra muy dura para los campesinos y para los pueblos indígenas.
examples.translation: It was a very hard war for the farmers and for the Indigenous peoples.

examples.text: Una comisión de la verdad estudió lo que pasó y dijo que murieron o desaparecieron más de doscientas mil personas.
examples.translation: A truth commission studied what happened and said that more than two hundred thousand people died or disappeared.

examples.text: En mil novecientos noventa y dos, Rigoberta Menchú, una mujer maya, ganó el Premio Nobel de la Paz.
examples.translation: In 1992, Rigoberta Menchú, a Maya woman, won the Nobel Peace Prize.

examples.text: El gobierno y los rebeldes firmaron los acuerdos de paz en diciembre de mil novecientos noventa y seis.
examples.translation: The government and the rebels signed the peace accords in December 1996.

examples.text: Hoy, muchas familias todavía buscan a sus desaparecidos.
examples.translation: Today, many families are still looking for their disappeared.

exercises.prompt: La guerra civil de Guatemala ___ en mil novecientos sesenta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Guatemala's civil war began in 1960.

exercises.prompt: Después de la guerra, una comisión de la verdad ___ lo que pasó.
exercises.promptTranslation: A truth commission studied what happened.

exercises.prompt: Más de doscientas mil personas ___ o desaparecieron.
exercises.promptTranslation: More than two hundred thousand people died or disappeared.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos noventa y dos, Rigoberta Menchú ___ el Premio Nobel de la Paz.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1992, Rigoberta Menchú won the Nobel Peace Prize.

exercises.prompt: En diciembre de mil novecientos noventa y seis, el gobierno y los rebeldes ___ los acuerdos de paz.
exercises.promptTranslation: The government and the rebels signed the peace accords.

exercises.prompt: Hoy, muchas familias todavía ___ a sus desaparecidos.
exercises.promptTranslation: Today, many families are still looking for their disappeared.

exercises.prompt: What did the truth commission report?
Who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992?
When were the peace accords signed?
exercises.explanation: Diciembre de mil novecientos noventa y seis.

lessons.title: 352. Reading: the Mexican Revolution
lessons.subtitle: Los campesinos querían tierra y libertad.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: Watch for the final sentence: it uses the passive se, which the news and history texts love.

examples.text: Porfirio Díaz gobernó México durante muchos años.
examples.translation: Porfirio Díaz governed Mexico for many years.

examples.text: En mil novecientos diez, Francisco Madero pidió elecciones libres y empezó la revolución.
examples.translation: In 1910, Francisco Madero asked for free elections and the revolution began.

examples.text: En el norte, Pancho Villa ganó muchos seguidores.
examples.translation: In the north, Pancho Villa won many followers.

examples.text: En el sur, Emiliano Zapata pidió tierras para los campesinos.
examples.translation: In the south, Emiliano Zapata asked for land for the farmers.

examples.text: Los campesinos querían tierra y libertad.
examples.translation: The farmers wanted land and freedom.

examples.text: La revolución duró muchos años y murió mucha gente.
examples.translation: The revolution lasted many years and many people died.

examples.text: En mil novecientos diecisiete se escribió una nueva constitución.
examples.translation: In 1917 a new constitution was written.

exercises.prompt: Porfirio Díaz ___ México durante muchos años.
exercises.promptTranslation: Porfirio Díaz governed Mexico for many years.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos diez, Madero ___ elecciones libres.
exercises.explanation: Dated event; pedir has e → i in the preterite.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1910, Madero asked for free elections.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos once, Zapata ___ tierras para los campesinos.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1911, Zapata asked for land for the farmers.

exercises.prompt: En esos años, los campesinos siempre ___ tierra y libertad.
exercises.explanation: Ongoing wish in the background → imperfect.
exercises.promptTranslation: In those years, the farmers wanted land and freedom.

exercises.prompt: La revolución ___ muchos años y murió mucha gente.
exercises.explanation: Completed period; the next verb is preterite.
exercises.promptTranslation: The revolution lasted many years and many people died.

exercises.prompt: En mil novecientos diecisiete se ___ una nueva constitución.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1917 a new constitution was written.

exercises.prompt: Who asked for free elections in 1910?
Where did Emiliano Zapata have his greatest support?
Which tense is “se escribió una constitución”?
options: The passive se in the preterite
exercises.explanation: Se + third person singular + singular thing.

lessons.title: 353. Reading: the War of the Pacific and Bolivia's coast
lessons.subtitle: Antes de la guerra, Bolivia tenía una costa.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: Here the imperfect sets the scene (before the war), and the preterite tells what changed.

examples.text: En mil ochocientos setenta y nueve empezó una guerra entre Chile, Bolivia y Perú.
examples.translation: In 1879 a war began between Chile, Bolivia and Peru.

examples.text: La guerra duró hasta mil ochocientos ochenta y cuatro.
examples.translation: The war lasted until 1884.

examples.text: Antes de la guerra, Bolivia tenía una costa en el océano Pacífico.
examples.translation: Before the war, Bolivia had a coast on the Pacific Ocean.

examples.text: Chile ganó la guerra y Bolivia perdió su costa.
examples.translation: Chile won the war and Bolivia lost its coast.

examples.text: Desde entonces, Bolivia no tiene salida al mar.
examples.translation: Since then, Bolivia has had no access to the sea.

examples.text: Cada año, los bolivianos recuerdan el Día del Mar y reclaman una salida al océano.
examples.translation: Every year, Bolivians remember the Day of the Sea and demand an outlet to the ocean.

examples.text: En dos mil dieciocho, un tribunal internacional decidió que Chile no estaba obligado a negociar.
examples.translation: In 2018, an international court decided that Chile was not obliged to negotiate.

exercises.prompt: En mil ochocientos setenta y nueve ___ una guerra entre Chile, Bolivia y Perú.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1879 a war began between Chile, Bolivia and Peru.

exercises.prompt: Antes de la guerra, Bolivia ___ una costa en el océano Pacífico.
exercises.explanation: Antes de... describes how things were → imperfect.
exercises.promptTranslation: Before the war, Bolivia had a coast on the Pacific Ocean.

exercises.prompt: Chile ganó la guerra y Bolivia ___ su costa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Chile won the war and Bolivia lost its coast.

exercises.prompt: Desde entonces, Bolivia no ___ salida al mar.
exercises.explanation: Desde entonces, still true today → present.
exercises.promptTranslation: Since then, Bolivia has had no access to the sea.

exercises.prompt: Hoy, cada año, los bolivianos ___ una salida al océano.
exercises.promptTranslation: Every year, Bolivians demand an outlet to the ocean.

exercises.prompt: En dos mil dieciocho, un tribunal internacional ___ que Chile no tenía que negociar.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 2018, an international court decided that Chile did not have to negotiate.

exercises.prompt: What did Bolivia lose in the war?
Which two verbs in this story are in the imperfect?
What did the 2018 court decide?
options: Chile did not have to negotiate access to the sea

lessons.title: 354. Reading: the war between Mexico and the United States
lessons.subtitle: México perdió más de la mitad de su territorio.

explanations.title: Un resumen de la historia
explanations.body: Notice the numbers: the years of the nineteenth century use mil ochocientos, with no y after mil.

examples.text: En mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis empezó una guerra entre México y Estados Unidos.
examples.translation: In 1846 a war began between Mexico and the United States.

examples.text: La causa principal fue el territorio: Estados Unidos quería California y las tierras del oeste.
examples.translation: The main cause was territory: the United States wanted California and the lands of the west.

examples.text: La guerra terminó en mil ochocientos cuarenta y ocho con el Tratado de Guadalupe Hidalgo.
examples.translation: The war ended in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

examples.text: México perdió más de la mitad de su territorio.
examples.translation: Mexico lost more than half of its territory.

examples.text: Muchas familias mexicanas se quedaron en esas tierras, y la frontera cambió para siempre.
examples.translation: Many Mexican families stayed on those lands, and the border changed forever.

examples.text: Hoy esas tierras forman parte de varios estados, como California, Nevada y Utah.
examples.translation: Today those lands are part of several states, such as California, Nevada and Utah.

exercises.prompt: En mil ochocientos cuarenta y seis ___ una guerra entre México y Estados Unidos.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 1846 a war began between Mexico and the United States.

exercises.prompt: Antes de la guerra, Estados Unidos ___ California y las tierras del oeste.
exercises.explanation: The wish behind the war → imperfect.
exercises.promptTranslation: The United States wanted California and the lands of the west.

exercises.prompt: La guerra ___ en mil ochocientos cuarenta y ocho.
exercises.promptTranslation: The war ended in 1848.

exercises.prompt: México ___ más de la mitad de su territorio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mexico lost more than half of its territory.

exercises.prompt: Después de la guerra, muchas familias mexicanas se ___ en esas tierras.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many Mexican families stayed on those lands.

exercises.prompt: La ___ entre México y Estados Unidos cambió para siempre.
exercises.promptTranslation: The border changed forever.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 1848?
options: mil y ochocientos cuarenta y ocho
un mil ochocientos cuarenta y ocho

exercises.prompt: What was the main cause of the war?
Why is “quería” imperfect and not preterite?
options: It describes a wish that lasted, not a single event
exercises.explanation: A wish or state that lasted, with no fixed end point, is usually imperfect.

lessons.title: 355. Saying years and dates in history
lessons.subtitle: En mil novecientos treinta y seis empezó la guerra.

explanations.title: Years are said as full numbers
explanations.body: In Spanish a year is read like any number, not in pairs. There is no y after mil, and you never split the year into pairs the way English does (“nineteen thirty-six”).

explanations.title: Dates
explanations.body: A date is el + day + de + month + de + year. The first of the month is el primero; every other day uses a cardinal number.

rows: el primero de enero de mil novecientos cincuenta y nueve
el dieciséis de septiembre de mil ochocientos diez
en diciembre de mil novecientos noventa y seis

exercises.prompt: La independencia de México empezó el dieciséis de septiembre de mil ___ diez.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mexico's independence began on September 16, 1810.

exercises.prompt: La Revolución mexicana empezó en mil ___ diez.
exercises.promptTranslation: The Mexican Revolution began in 1910.

exercises.prompt: Batista salió del país el ___ de enero.
exercises.explanation: The first of the month: el primero.
exercises.promptTranslation: Batista left the country on the first of January.

exercises.prompt: El acuerdo de paz se firmó en mil novecientos noventa y ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: The peace accord was signed in 1996.

exercises.prompt: En dos ___ dieciocho, un tribunal tomó una decisión.
exercises.explanation: Dos mil: mil does not take an s after a number.
exercises.promptTranslation: In 2018, a court made a decision.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 1936?
options: mil novecientos y treinta y seis
un mil novecientos treinta y seis
exercises.explanation: No y after mil; no pairs.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 2018?
Which is 1959?
Which date uses the ordinal?
exercises.explanation: Only the first of the month is ordinal.

lessons.title: 356. Cause, result and sequence in a story
lessons.subtitle: Hubo una crisis; por eso, mucha gente protestó.

explanations.title: Little words that hold a history together
explanations.body: Good history writing links events. These expressions say why something happened, what followed, or in what order.

rows: A causa de la crisis, el gobierno cayó.
Hubo una crisis; por eso, mucha gente protestó.
No había trabajo; por lo tanto, muchos se fueron.
Primero hubo elecciones; luego, un golpe.
Después de la guerra, firmaron la paz.
A pesar de la guerra, la gente siguió trabajando.

exercises.prompt: Hubo una crisis; ___, mucha gente protestó.
exercises.promptTranslation: There was a crisis; that is why many people protested.

exercises.prompt: Mucha gente protestó ___ no tenía trabajo.
exercises.promptTranslation: Many people protested because they had no work.

exercises.prompt: ___ la crisis, el gobierno cayó.
exercises.promptTranslation: Because of the crisis, the government fell.

exercises.prompt: Primero hubo elecciones; ___, hubo un golpe.
exercises.promptTranslation: First there were elections; then there was a coup.

exercises.prompt: Después de muchos años de guerra, ___ se firmó la paz.
exercises.promptTranslation: After many years of war, peace was finally signed.

exercises.prompt: No había trabajo; ___, muchos se fueron del país.
exercises.promptTranslation: There was no work; therefore, many left the country.

exercises.prompt: Which expression means “despite”?
Which one can be followed directly by a noun and means “because of”?
exercises.explanation: Porque needs a verb clause; a causa de takes a noun.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence puts the events in order?
options: Finalmente hubo elecciones; primero, un golpe.
Luego hubo un golpe; primero, hubo elecciones.
Primero hubo elecciones; luego, hubo un golpe.
Después de hubo elecciones, un golpe.

lessons.title: 357. History in the passive: fue firmado or se firmó
lessons.subtitle: El tratado fue firmado; se firmó la paz.

explanations.title: Two ways to avoid naming the doer
explanations.body: Histories use the complete passive (ser + participle + por) when the doer matters, and the passive se when it does not. In the complete passive the participle agrees with the thing; in the passive se the verb agrees with the thing.

Las tierras fueron repartidas entre los campesinos.

Las fronteras fueron cerradas por el gobierno.
La constitución fue escrita en mil novecientos diecisiete.

lessons.title: 359. Reading: the Taíno people
lessons.subtitle: Los taínos vivían en las islas del Caribe.

explanations.title: Describing a way of life: the imperfect
explanations.body: When you describe how people lived in a time long ago, the imperfect is the natural tense. Notice how almost every verb here describes habits, jobs and surroundings; the one single event, the arrival of the Europeans, is in the preterite.

examples.text: Los taínos vivían en las islas del Caribe antes de la llegada de los europeos.

examples.translation: They also fished in the sea and hunted birds.

examples.translation: The Taíno really liked playing ball in a space called a batey.

lessons.title: 365. A police report: active, passive and se
lessons.subtitle: La policía detuvo a los ladrones.

explanations.title: Same event, three sentences
explanations.body: A police report can choose how to present the same event. The active names the doer first; the complete passive puts the receiver first; the passive se hides the doer.

rows: La policía detuvo a los ladrones.
Los ladrones fueron detenidos por la policía.
La calle fue cerrada por la policía.
Un juez condenó a los asaltantes.
Los asaltantes fueron condenados por un juez.
El dinero fue robado por los ladrones.
tables.note: With a personal a (a los ladrones), the se is impersonal and the verb stays singular in standard Spanish.

exercises.prompt: La policía detuvo a los ladrones. = Los ladrones fueron ___ por la policía.
exercises.promptTranslation: The police arrested the robbers. = The robbers were arrested by the police.

exercises.promptTranslation: A judge sentenced the robbers. = The robbers were sentenced by a judge.

exercises.prompt: La policía cerró la calle. = La calle fue ___ por la policía.
exercises.promptTranslation: The police closed the street. = The street was closed by the police.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ a los ladrones.
exercises.explanation: Personal a keeps the verb singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: The robbers were arrested.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ el dinero que robaron.
exercises.promptTranslation: The money they stole was recovered.

exercises.prompt: Se ___ las calles cerca del banco.

explanations.title: A mysterious life, told in the present
explanations.body: Biographers often switch to the present to make the past feel immediate. Most verbs here refer to the past, but are conjugated in the present.

lessons.title: 372. Review: the accidental se and the passive se

explanations.title: Two different ses
explanations.body: The accidental se says that something happened to someone: se + indirect pronoun + verb agreeing with the thing. The passive se hides the doer: se + verb agreeing with the thing, with no indirect pronoun. When the object is a specific person with the personal a, the se is impersonal and the verb stays singular: Se detuvo a los ladrones.

lessons.title: 375. Aches and pains: me duele…
lessons.subtitle: Me duele la cabeza y tengo fiebre.

explanations.title: Doler works like gustar
explanations.body: To say that something hurts, Spanish uses doler with an indirect pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les). The part of the body is the subject, so the verb agrees with it: one thing, duele; more than one, duelen. To name a symptom, use tener: tengo fiebre, tengo tos, tengo náuseas.

lessons.title: 378. Haber: he, has, ha, hemos, han
lessons.subtitle: Yo he comido. Ellos han llegado.

explanations.title: A helper verb
explanations.body: Haber is the helper (auxiliary) verb that builds the perfect tenses. It is not the same as tener: tener means to own or to hold, while haber just helps another verb. Its present-tense forms are irregular, so memorize them.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have eaten.

lessons.title: 379. The present perfect: haber + participle
lessons.subtitle: Hoy he trabajado mucho y hemos comido tarde.

explanations.title: Forming it
explanations.body: The present perfect is haber in the present plus the past participle: -ado for -ar verbs, -ido for -er and -ir verbs. The participle never changes, no matter who the subject is. It describes something that happened in a period that is not over yet (hoy, esta semana, este año), or something with a result that matters now.

examples.translation: This week I have worked a lot.

explanations.title: Pronouns stand before haber
explanations.body: Object and reflexive pronouns go in front of haber, never between haber and the participle, and never after the participle. No also goes in front of the pronouns: No lo he visto. Two pronouns go together before haber, and le/les change to se before lo, la, los, las.

I have told it to him.
Have they given it to you?

explanations.title: Small words that go with the perfect
explanations.body: These words usually go before haber (and before any pronouns): Ya he comido. Todavía no he llegado. Todavía can also come at the end (No he llegado todavía). Putting them between haber and the participle (he ya comido) is much less common, so learn the pattern ya + haber.

lessons.title: 383. Present perfect or preterite?
lessons.subtitle: Ayer fui al médico. Esta semana he tenido fiebre.

explanations.title: Finished time, or time that is still open?
explanations.body: A time word that points to a finished period (ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, hace tres años) calls for the preterite. The present perfect fits periods that are not over (hoy, esta semana, este año) and experiences with no date (nunca, alguna vez, ya). Be aware that speakers differ: in Spain the perfect is common for the recent past (Esta mañana he desayunado fruta), while in much of Latin America people say Esta mañana desayuné fruta. Both are normal. What never works is the perfect with a finished time word: not ayer he ido.

rows: Hace tres años mi abuelo estuvo en el hospital.
perfecto (ya also takes the preterite in much of Latin America: Ya comí)

lessons.title: 384. Ha habido: there has been

explanations.title: Impersonal haber has one form
explanations.body: When haber means “there is / there are”, it never changes for singular or plural: hay, hubo, había, ha habido. So you say Ha habido tres accidentes, not Han habido tres accidentes.

rows: Hay un accidente en la carretera.
Ayer hubo un accidente en la carretera.
Cuando llegamos, ya había mucha gente.
Esta semana ha habido tres accidentes.

lessons.title: 385. How have you been?

explanations.title: Greeting an old friend with the perfect
explanations.body: When you have not seen someone for a while, the present perfect is the natural tense for catching up. With usted, the questions use ha: ¿Cómo ha estado usted?

rows: ¿Cómo te ha ido en el trabajo?

explanations.body: To say how you or others have been, use haber + estado + an adjective. The adjective agrees with the person, but estado never changes.

lessons.subtitle: Las autoridades han informado de un aumento de los casos.

explanations.body: News reports use the present perfect to bring recent events to the reader’s present: the authorities have reported, the cases have risen. Read the article, then try the exercises.

explanations.title: Health advice in the formal command
explanations.body: Public-health advice addresses the reader as usted (one person) or ustedes (a group). Review: drop the -o of the yo form and add -e / -en for -ar verbs, -a / -an for -er and -ir verbs. Pronouns attach to an affirmative command and go before a negative one.

rows: Evite el contacto con personas enfermas.
Quédese en casa si tiene fiebre.
Stay home if you have a fever.
Drink a lot of water and rest.
No comparta los vasos ni los platos.

lessons.title: 389. The doctor’s orders: commands with pronouns

explanations.title: Take it, give it, don’t give it
explanations.body: On a prescription label or in a doctor’s office, orders come with pronouns for the medicine or the patient. Remember: in an affirmative command the pronouns attach to the verb and an accent mark keeps the stress; in a negative command they stand in front. When le or les meets lo or la, it becomes se.

No me diga que no le duele.
No se la dé al niño.

explanations.title: Where the water is
explanations.body: Rivers are born (nacer) in the mountains and end (desembocar) in the sea. A bay is a part of the sea that cuts into the coast; an island is land surrounded by water; a peninsula is land surrounded by water on three sides.

El lago es profundo y frío.
El océano Pacífico es el más grande.

lessons.title: 394. Where is it? Located, bordered, between
lessons.subtitle: Chile está situado entre los Andes y el océano Pacífico.

explanations.title: Describing where a place is
explanations.body: Besides estar, geography uses está situado/ubicado, se encuentra, queda, and limita con (it borders). Situado and ubicado are adjectives, so they agree with the thing: una ciudad ubicada, un país situado.

Bolivia borders Peru, Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Chile.
Quito se encuentra en el norte del Ecuador.
Quito is in the north of Ecuador.
El volcán queda al oeste de la ciudad.
The volcano is west of the city.

lessons.title: 402. The past perfect: había + participle
lessons.subtitle: Yo ya había comido. Ellos habían llegado.

explanations.title: Forming the past perfect
explanations.body: The past perfect (el pluscuamperfecto) is haber in the imperfect plus the past participle. It works just like the present perfect, but the helper is in the past. The participle never changes.

exercises.prompt: Yo ya ___ comido cuando llegaste.
exercises.promptTranslation: I had already eaten when you arrived.

exercises.prompt: Tú ya ___ salido cuando llamé.
exercises.promptTranslation: You had already left when I called.

exercises.prompt: Nosotros ya ___ terminado el trabajo.
exercises.promptTranslation: We had already finished the work.

exercises.prompt: Ellos ya ___ llegado al hospital.
exercises.promptTranslation: They had already arrived at the hospital.

exercises.prompt: Vosotros ya ___ hablado con el médico.
exercises.promptTranslation: You (all) had already spoken with the doctor.

exercises.prompt: Mi abuela había ___ en esa casa toda su vida.
exercises.promptTranslation: My grandmother had lived in that house all her life.

exercises.prompt: Los científicos ya habían ___ el estudio.
exercises.promptTranslation: The scientists had already finished the study.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between he comido and había comido?

lessons.title: 403. The past perfect: the earlier of two past events
lessons.subtitle: Cuando llegué, el tren ya había salido.

explanations.title: Before something else in the past
explanations.body: Use the past perfect for an action that was completed before another past moment. Two past events: the one that happened first goes in the past perfect, and the later one is often in the preterite.

rows: The train had already left when I arrived.
We had already eaten when they called.
el médico ya había hablado con ella
The doctor had already spoken with her when I came in.
They had explored the jungle when the new expedition arrived.

exercises.prompt: Cuando llegamos al hospital, el médico ya ___ salido.
exercises.explanation: An earlier past event → past perfect.
exercises.promptTranslation: When we arrived at the hospital, the doctor had already left.

exercises.prompt: Cuando llegué a la clase, mis amigos ya ___ empezado.
exercises.promptTranslation: When I arrived at class, my friends had already started.

exercises.prompt: Antes de ir a Chile, yo nunca ___ visto una montaña tan alta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Before going to Chile, I had never seen such a tall mountain.

exercises.promptTranslation: When you called, we had already eaten.

lessons.title: 404. The past perfect: negatives, pronouns and little words

explanations.title: Same rules as the present perfect
explanations.body: No goes before haber; pronouns also go before haber; ya, todavía, nunca and antes usually go before haber (or at the end of the sentence). Avoid putting them between haber and the participle.

rows: I had never seen a jungle.
La selva: ya la habían explorado antes.
The jungle: they had already explored it before.
Le había escrito una carta al presidente.
I had written the president a letter.
I had written it to him.

lessons.title: 405. Past perfect or preterite?
lessons.subtitle: Ya había estudiado cuando empezó el examen, y por eso lo hice bien.

explanations.title: Which one came first?
explanations.body: A story in the past gives its events in order using the preterite. When you step back to something that was already done before the moment you are describing, use the past perfect.

rows: Primero estudié y luego hice el examen.
A ya estaba hecho cuando B
Ya había estudiado cuando empezó el examen.
Antes del examen, había estudiado mucho.

exercises.explanation: A sequence of finished events: preterite.

lessons.title: 407. Three ways to talk about the future
lessons.subtitle: Voy a viajar. Viajo mañana. Viajaré el año próximo.

explanations.title: Ir a, the present, and the simple future
explanations.body: Spanish has three common ways to talk about what comes next. Ir a + infinitive is the everyday choice for plans you feel sure about. The present tense works for scheduled or very near events, with a time word. The simple future (viajaré, tendré) states strong intentions, promises, dreams and predictions.

rows: Voy a viajar a Chile el año próximo.
I am going to travel to Chile next year.
Compraré una casa en cuatro años.
I will buy a house in four years.
Me casaré y tendré dos hijos.
I will get married and have two children.

exercises.prompt: Mañana yo ___ a visitar el volcán.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow I am going to visit the volcano.

exercises.prompt: Dentro de cuatro años yo ___ una casa.
exercises.explanation: A plan stated with the simple future.
exercises.promptTranslation: In four years I will buy a house.

exercises.prompt: Mañana por la mañana yo ___ mi tarea.
exercises.explanation: The present can talk about the near future with a time word.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow morning I finish my homework.

exercises.prompt: El año próximo nosotros ___ a Chile.
exercises.promptTranslation: Next year we will travel to Chile.

exercises.prompt: Mis padres ___ en esta casa toda la vida; es una promesa.
exercises.promptTranslation: My parents will live in this house all their lives; it is a promise.

exercises.prompt: Esta noche voy a ___ para el examen.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tonight I am going to study for the exam.

exercises.prompt: Which form states a strong intention or promise?

lessons.title: 408. The future of probability: I wonder…
lessons.subtitle: ¿Dónde estará Héctor? Estará jugando videojuegos.

explanations.title: When the future is about now
explanations.body: The simple future can also express a guess or a doubt about the present. It is the Spanish way of saying “I wonder” or “probably”. A plain question or statement uses the present (¿Dónde está Héctor?). The future adds the idea of speculation: ¿Dónde estará Héctor? Estará jugando videojuegos.

rows: I wonder where Héctor is. He is probably playing video games.
I wonder who that woman is. She is probably a lawyer or a judge.
I wonder what Luisa is doing. She is probably studying for her exam.

exercises.prompt: Son las nueve y Marta no contesta el teléfono. ¿Dónde ___?
exercises.promptTranslation: It is nine and Marta does not answer the phone. Where can she be?

exercises.prompt: Héctor no está en casa. Seguramente ___ jugando videojuegos en casa de un amigo.
exercises.promptTranslation: Héctor is not at home. He is probably playing video games at a friend’s house.

exercises.prompt: ¿Quién ___ esa mujer que está ahora en la puerta? Nunca la he visto.
exercises.promptTranslation: Who can that woman be? I have never seen her.

exercises.prompt: Esa mujer lleva un traje elegante; ___ abogada o jueza.
exercises.promptTranslation: That woman wears an elegant suit; she is probably a lawyer or a judge.

exercises.prompt: El paciente tiene fiebre alta; ___ una infección.
exercises.promptTranslation: The patient has a high fever; he probably has an infection.

exercises.prompt: No sé cuántos años tiene mi vecino. ___ unos cincuenta.
exercises.promptTranslation: I don’t know how old my neighbor is. He is probably around fifty.

exercises.prompt: What does “¿Dónde estará Héctor?” express?

lessons.title: 409. Wondering aloud: more probability
lessons.subtitle: ¿Cuánto costará? Habrá mucha gente en el hospital.

explanations.title: Same idea, other verbs
explanations.body: The future of probability works with any verb. Irregular future stems still apply: habrá (there must be), podrá, sabrá, dirá. For doing-right-now guesses, use estar + gerund: estará durmiendo.

rows: It probably costs about twenty pesos.
There must be a lot of people; it is Saturday.
He is probably tired or sick.
I wonder how old the doctor is. He is probably about forty.

lessons.title: 410. The conditional: regular verbs

explanations.title: Would + verb
explanations.body: The conditional says what would happen or what someone would do. Like the future, it is formed by adding endings to the whole infinitive: -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Spanish does not need a separate word for “would”.

exercises.promptTranslation: In his place, I would drink more water.

exercises.promptTranslation: In your place, they would not spend so much money.

exercises.prompt: En tu lugar, yo ___ al médico.

lessons.title: 411. The conditional: irregular stems
lessons.subtitle: En tu lugar, yo diría la verdad y saldría temprano.

explanations.title: The same twelve stems as the future
explanations.body: The verbs that are irregular in the future are irregular in the conditional in exactly the same way. Add the conditional endings to these stems.

exercises.promptTranslation: In your place, I would tell the truth.

explanations.title: Softening what you say
explanations.body: The conditional makes requests and advice sound polite and less direct. Podría is much softer than puedo; me gustaría is softer than quiero; debería is softer than debo.

rows: Could you tell me where the hospital is?
Me gustaría hablar con el médico.
I would like to talk with the doctor.
If I were you, I would rest.
Would you mind opening the window?

exercises.promptTranslation: Excuse me, sir, could you tell me where the hospital is?

exercises.prompt: Me ___ hablar con el médico, por favor.

It puts it in the past

lessons.title: 413. Would: conditional or imperfect?
lessons.subtitle: De niño, iba al río. Hoy iría, pero estoy cansado.

explanations.title: Two meanings of “would”
explanations.body: English uses “would” for two different ideas. For something you used to do again and again in the past, Spanish uses the imperfect. For what would happen or what someone would do under some condition, Spanish uses the conditional. The conditional also reports what someone said would happen: Dijo que vendría mañana.

rows: De niño, siempre iba al río.
Todos los sábados íbamos al mercado.

lessons.title: 415. Se review: reflexive and reciprocal
lessons.subtitle: Yo me despierto a las siete. Los alumnos se miraron.

explanations.title: Same pronouns, different jobs
explanations.body: The pronouns me, te, se, nos, os show up again and again. Se is the form for the third person (usted, él, ella, ustedes, ellos, ellas). With a reflexive verb, the action returns to the subject: Yo me despierto. With a reciprocal meaning, two or more people act on each other: Los alumnos se miraron (they looked at each other). This normally needs a plural (or collective) subject.

rows: Yo me despierto a las siete.
Mauricio se despierta a las ocho.
The students looked at each other.
We said goodbye to each other.

exercises.prompt: Yo ___ despierto a las siete.
exercises.promptTranslation: I wake up at seven.

exercises.prompt: Mauricio ___ despierta a las ocho.
exercises.promptTranslation: Mauricio wakes up at eight.

exercises.prompt: Tú ___ levantas muy temprano.

exercises.promptTranslation: We see each other every day.

lessons.title: 416. Se review: se lo, and the impersonal se
lessons.subtitle: Se lo regalé ayer. ¿Qué se puede hacer?

explanations.title: Se instead of le or les, and se for “one”
explanations.body: Before lo, la, los, las, the pronouns le and les become se: Le regalé un perro a mi madre → Se lo regalé. Impersonal se talks about people in general, with no one in particular: ¿Qué se puede hacer? Se vive bien aquí. The verb stays in the third-person singular.

rows: Le regalé un perro a mi madre.
I gave my mother a dog.
I gave it to her yesterday.
Les pagué el peaje. Se lo pagué todo.
I paid them the toll. I paid it all to them.
En esta ciudad se vive bien.
One lives well in this city.

exercises.promptTranslation: I already paid the employees the money.

lessons.title: 417. Se review: the passive se and the accidental se

explanations.title: Two se-constructions with the noun as subject
explanations.body: The passive se names no doer: Se explotaron los recursos naturales (the resources were exploited). The verb agrees with the noun that follows. The accidental se adds an indirect pronoun to show who it happened to: A Tanya se le cayó el libro.

rows: Se desviaron varios ríos para construir la presa.
Several rivers were diverted to build the dam.
A Tanya se le cayó el libro.

no noun to agree with, or a person with the personal a

lessons.title: 419. Defending the land: key words
lessons.subtitle: Los defensores del medio ambiente protegen el territorio de sus comunidades.

explanations.title: Words for people who protect nature
explanations.body: Many people in Latin America defend rivers, forests and land, often at great personal risk. These are the words you will meet in stories about them.

La comunidad vive junto al río.

El territorio de la comunidad es sagrado para ella.

La empresa quería explotar el oro.
to report, to speak out against

lessons.title: 420. Reading: Berta Cáceres and the Lenca people
lessons.subtitle: Berta Cáceres defendió el río Gualcarque y ganó un premio internacional.

explanations.title: A leader who defended a river
explanations.body: This text is a factual summary. Read it, then answer the questions.

explanations.body: The past perfect steps back from a moment in the past (había + participle). The future looks ahead (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án), and the same forms can express a guess about the present.

lessons.title: 428. Fires and drought
lessons.subtitle: La sequía, el calor y el viento ayudan a que el fuego se extienda.

explanations.title: Why wildfires spread
explanations.body: Wildfires need dry land, heat and wind. When the ground and the plants are dry after a drought, a small fire can become very large in a few hours.

rows: El fuego se movió rápido por el viento.
Los bomberos trabajaron día y noche.
El bosque se quemó en tres días.
El fuego se extendió por el viento.

exercises.prompt: El ___ cubrió el cielo y casi no se veía el sol.
exercises.promptTranslation: The smoke covered the sky and the sun could hardly be seen.

exercises.promptTranslation: The firefighters worked day and night.

exercises.promptTranslation: The fire spread quickly because of the wind.

exercises.prompt: Con la tierra tan ___, el fuego avanza muy rápido.
exercises.promptTranslation: With the ground so dry, the fire advances very fast.

exercises.promptTranslation: The firefighters put out the fire after two days.

lessons.title: 429. After the disaster: damage and victims
lessons.subtitle: Hubo heridos, desaparecidos y miles de personas sin casa.

explanations.title: Describing the aftermath
explanations.body: After a disaster, reports count what was lost and who needs help. Herido (injured), muerto (dead) and desaparecido (missing) are participles used as nouns: with haber (hubo heridos) they say how many people were affected, and like any noun they can be the subject or object of other verbs (buscan a los desaparecidos).

rows: Hubo muchos heridos en el hospital.
Los sobrevivientes pasaron la noche afuera.
Miles de damnificados perdieron su casa.
Los rescatistas buscan entre los escombros.

exercises.promptTranslation: The damage was enormous: many houses were destroyed.

exercises.promptTranslation: They are still searching for the missing among the rubble.

exercises.promptTranslation: The rebuilding of the houses took several years.

exercises.prompt: Which word means “missing person”?

lessons.title: 430. Rescue and relief

explanations.title: Helping after a disaster
explanations.body: Rescue teams look for people; volunteers and governments deliver aid. These are the words for who does what and what they bring.

El equipo de rescate llegó en una hora.
Cientos de voluntarios ayudaron a limpiar.
Las donaciones llegaron de muchos países.

Las familias durmieron en un albergue.
La ayuda humanitaria llegó por avión.

lessons.title: 431. Reading: Chile, 1960, the strongest earthquake ever recorded
lessons.subtitle: El terremoto de Valdivia tuvo la magnitud más alta que se ha registrado.

explanations.title: A giant earthquake in the south of Chile
explanations.body: Read a short account, then answer the questions.

examples.text: El veintidós de mayo de mil novecientos sesenta, un terremoto sacudió el sur de Chile.
examples.translation: On May 22, 1960, an earthquake shook the south of Chile.

examples.text: Se llama el terremoto de Valdivia, por la ciudad que sufrió grandes daños.
examples.translation: It is called the Valdivia earthquake, after the city that suffered great damage.

examples.text: Su magnitud fue de nueve punto cinco, la más alta que se ha registrado en el mundo.
examples.translation: Its magnitude was 9.5, the highest ever recorded in the world.

examples.text: La tierra tembló durante varios minutos y muchas casas se cayeron.

examples.translation: The waves reached Hawaii and Japan and caused more damage.

exercises.promptTranslation: The ground shook for several minutes.

exercises.promptTranslation: The earthquake caused a tsunami that crossed the Pacific Ocean.

exercises.promptTranslation: The waves reached Hawaii and Japan.

exercises.promptTranslation: Many people were left without a home.

It was the lowest ever recorded

lessons.title: 432. Reading: Hurricane María in Puerto Rico
lessons.subtitle: El huracán María dejó a toda la isla sin electricidad.

explanations.title: A hurricane, two weeks after another one
explanations.body: Puerto Rico was hit by two major hurricanes in September 2017. The past perfect and the preterite together tell the story.

examples.text: Dos semanas antes, el huracán Irma ya había pasado cerca de Puerto Rico.
examples.translation: Two weeks earlier, Hurricane Irma had already passed near Puerto Rico.

examples.text: El veinte de septiembre de dos mil diecisiete, el huracán María llegó a la isla con vientos muy fuertes.
examples.translation: On September 20, 2017, Hurricane María reached the island with very strong winds.

examples.text: El viento destruyó casas, árboles y líneas eléctricas, y las lluvias causaron inundaciones.
examples.translation: The wind destroyed houses, trees and power lines, and the rains caused floods.

examples.text: Toda la isla se quedó sin electricidad, y en algunos lugares la luz tardó meses en volver.
examples.translation: The whole island lost power, and in some places the electricity took months to return.

examples.text: Mucha gente no podía llamar por teléfono ni comprar comida.
examples.translation: Many people could not make phone calls or buy food.

examples.text: Más tarde, el gobierno reconoció que murieron casi tres mil personas durante los meses siguientes.
examples.translation: Later, the government recognized that almost three thousand people died in the following months.

examples.text: La ayuda llegó de otros estados y de muchos voluntarios.
examples.translation: Aid arrived from other states and from many volunteers.

exercises.prompt: Dos semanas antes, el huracán Irma ya ___ pasado cerca de la isla.
exercises.promptTranslation: Two weeks earlier, Hurricane Irma had already passed near the island.

lessons.title: 433. Reading: the Volcán de Fuego in Guatemala
lessons.subtitle: El volcán de Fuego hizo erupción el tres de junio de dos mil dieciocho.

explanations.title: When a volcano erupts
explanations.body: The Volcán de Fuego is one of the most active volcanoes in Central America. Read about its eruption in 2018.

examples.text: El Volcán de Fuego, en Guatemala, es uno de los volcanes más activos de América.
examples.translation: The Volcán de Fuego, in Guatemala, is one of the most active volcanoes in the Americas.

examples.text: El tres de junio de dos mil dieciocho, tuvo una erupción muy fuerte.

lessons.title: 434. Reading: wildfires in northern Argentina
lessons.subtitle: En dos mil veintidós el fuego destruyó una gran parte de los Esteros del Iberá.

explanations.title: Fire in the wetlands
explanations.body: In early 2022, large fires burned in the province of Corrientes, in northeastern Argentina. Read what happened and why it spread.

lessons.title: 435. Reading disaster headlines
lessons.subtitle: Un terremoto sacude la costa. Se registran réplicas.

explanations.title: How headlines are written
explanations.body: Headlines are short. They often use the present tense to report something that just happened (the historical present), the passive se, and the present perfect with ha(n) + participle.

rows: Cierran el puerto por el huracán
Port closed because of the hurricane
A hundred families have been evacuated
El gobierno declara el estado de emergencia
The government declares a state of emergency
Ha habido daños en las carreteras
There has been damage to the roads

exercises.prompt: Un terremoto ___ la costa.
exercises.promptTranslation: An earthquake shakes the coast.

exercises.promptTranslation: The authorities are closing the port because of the hurricane.

exercises.prompt: Han sido ___ cien familias.
exercises.promptTranslation: A hundred families have been evacuated.

exercises.prompt: Ha ___ daños en las carreteras.
exercises.promptTranslation: There has been damage to the roads.

exercises.promptTranslation: The government declares a state of emergency.

Because they are about the future
It makes the news feel immediate

What does “Han sido evacuadas cien familias” tell us?

lessons.title: 436. Formal commands: the regular pattern
lessons.subtitle: Camine despacio. Lea las instrucciones. Escriba su nombre.

explanations.title: A quick review
explanations.body: To give an order to one person you address as usted, take the yo form of the present, drop the -o, and add the opposite vowel: -ar verbs take -e; -er and -ir verbs take -a. For ustedes, add -n. Verbs ending in -car, -gar and -zar change their spelling to keep the sound: buscar → busque, pagar → pague, empezar → empiece.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ despacio por las escaleras.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, walk slowly down the stairs.

exercises.prompt: Señor, ___ las instrucciones antes de entrar.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, read the instructions before going in.

exercises.prompt: Señores, ___ su nombre en esta lista.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, write your name on this list.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ aquí un momento, por favor.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, wait here a moment, please.

exercises.prompt: Señor, ___ la puerta con cuidado.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, open the door carefully.

exercises.prompt: Señores, ___ en el refugio hasta que termine la tormenta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, eat in the shelter until the storm ends.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ a sus hijos en el refugio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, look for your children in the shelter.

exercises.prompt: Which vowel do -ar verbs take in the formal command?
How do you form the ustedes command?

lessons.title: 437. Formal commands: verbs with an irregular yo form
lessons.subtitle: Salga de la casa. Traiga agua. Tenga calma.

explanations.title: The yo form decides
explanations.body: A verb whose yo form is irregular (digo, hago, oigo, pongo, salgo, tengo, traigo, vengo) keeps that irregularity in every command form; the exceptions (dar, estar, ir, saber, ser) come in a later lesson. If you know digo, hago, oigo, pongo, salgo, tengo, traigo, vengo, you already know diga, haga, oiga, ponga, salga, tenga, traiga, venga.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ de la casa por la puerta principal.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, leave the house through the main door.

exercises.prompt: Señor, ___ agua potable al refugio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, bring drinking water to the shelter.

exercises.prompt: Señores, ___ calma y sigan al guía.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, stay calm and follow the guide.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ sus documentos en una bolsa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, put your documents in a bag.

exercises.prompt: Señores, ___ fila y esperen su turno.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, form a line and wait your turn.

exercises.prompt: Señor, ___ al refugio ahora mismo.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, come to the shelter right now.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ bien el aviso que da la radio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, listen carefully to the notice on the radio.

exercises.prompt: What is the usted command of decir?
Why is it “traiga” and not “traya”?
options: Because it is a regular verb
Because it is a plural command
Because it is a reflexive verb
Because the yo form is traigo
exercises.explanation: The command keeps the irregularity of the yo form.

lessons.title: 438. Formal commands: stem-changing verbs
lessons.subtitle: Piense con calma. Pida ayuda. Vuelva después.

explanations.title: Boots stay in the command
explanations.body: A verb with a stem change in the present (ie, ue, i) keeps it in the usted and ustedes commands. It does not appear in the nosotros command of -ar and -er verbs, but you will see that later.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ con calma y salga ordenadamente.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, think calmly and leave in an orderly way.

exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, turn on the radio to listen to the news.

exercises.prompt: Señor, ___ ayuda a los bomberos.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, ask the firefighters for help.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ si ya tenemos luz.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, check whether we already have power.

exercises.prompt: Señores, no ___ a la zona del desastre.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, do not go back to the disaster zone.

exercises.prompt: Señor, no ___ de miedo; todo está controlado.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, do not tremble with fear; everything is under control.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ las ventanas antes de salir.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, close the windows before you leave.

exercises.prompt: What is the usted command of repetir?
What happens to the stem of volver in the command?

lessons.title: 439. Formal commands: ser, estar, dar, ir, saber
lessons.subtitle: Sea paciente. Esté atento. Dé la alerta. Vaya al refugio.

explanations.title: Five verbs that follow no pattern
explanations.body: These five verbs have commands you must memorize. Note the accent mark on dé (to tell it apart from the preposition de) and on esté and estén.

exercises.prompt: Señora, ___ paciente: el equipo de rescate llegará pronto.

exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, give the alert to your neighbors.

exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, give a flashlight to each family.

exercises.promptTranslation: Ma’am, go to the shelter by the main street.

exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, know where the nearest exit is.

exercises.prompt: Why does the usted command of dar have an accent?
options: Because it is a past tense
To tell it apart from the preposition de

exercises.prompt: What is the ustedes command of ir?

lessons.title: 440. Negative formal commands: what not to do
lessons.subtitle: No use el ascensor. No toque los cables. No corra.

explanations.title: No + the command
explanations.body: To say what not to do, put no in front of the command. Everything else is the same: the same stem changes, the same spelling changes. Safety posters are full of these.

rows: No vuelva a la zona de peligro.
Do not go back to the danger zone.

exercises.prompt: Durante un terremoto, señora, no ___ el ascensor.
exercises.promptTranslation: During an earthquake, do not use the elevator.

exercises.prompt: Señor, no ___ a los demás; hay espacio para todos.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, do not push others; there is room for everyone.

exercises.prompt: Señores, no ___ a la zona de peligro.

options: At the end of the sentence

lessons.title: 441. Formal commands with pronouns
lessons.subtitle: Désela. Cúbrase la cabeza. No se la dé. No se cubra.

explanations.title: Attach after, place before
explanations.body: In an affirmative command, pronouns attach to the end of the verb, and a written accent mark keeps the stress where it was. In a negative command, they stand in front of the verb, as always. With two pronouns, indirect comes first (se, me, te, le) and direct second (lo, la, los, las); le and les become se.

exercises.prompt: Durante el temblor, ___ la cabeza con los brazos.
exercises.explanation: Affirmative: attach se and accent the stressed syllable.
exercises.promptTranslation: During the quake, cover your head with your arms.

exercises.prompt: Hace frío: ___ una chaqueta, por favor.
exercises.explanation: Affirmative: attach se and add the accent.
exercises.promptTranslation: It is cold: put on a jacket, please.

exercises.prompt: La luz, señora, ___ antes de salir.
exercises.explanation: Affirmative: attach la and add the accent.
exercises.promptTranslation: The light, ma’am, turn it off before leaving.

exercises.promptTranslation: The cables, sir, do not touch them.

exercises.prompt: La noticia, señor, no ___ diga a los niños todavía.

exercises.prompt: Why does “cúbrase” have an accent mark?
options: To keep the stress on the same syllable

exercises.prompt: Which pronoun goes first with two pronouns?
Which sentence is correct?

lessons.title: 442. Safety instructions: before an earthquake
lessons.subtitle: Prepare un kit de emergencia y practique el simulacro con su familia.

explanations.title: Prepare ahead
explanations.body: Public safety leaflets give orders to the reader as usted or ustedes. Read these before-the-quake instructions, then use the same forms in the exercises.

rows: Guarde agua y comida para varios días.
Store water and food for several days.
Identifique las salidas de su casa.
Identify the exits of your home.

explanations.title: Forming the “let’s” command
explanations.body: Start with the yo form of the present, drop the -o, and add -emos for -ar verbs and -amos for -er and -ir verbs. The affirmative and negative are the same: Visitemos el museo. No visitemos el museo. -ar and -er verbs with a stem change in the present do not change here (pensemos, volvamos), but -ir verbs do change (pidamos, durmamos).

For “let’s go” people usually use vamos (affirmative), and no vayamos (negative); vayamos also appears in formal speech.

explanations.title: Attach after, place before
explanations.body: As with the usted command, pronouns attach to an affirmative nosotros command with an accent on the stressed syllable, and go in front of a negative one. The final -s of the verb is dropped before nos or se (reflexive nos or se, or se replacing le/les): levantemos + nos → levantémonos; digamos + se + lo → digámoselo. (Irregular: vamos + nos → vámonos.)

explanations.title: Take the usted command and add -s
explanations.body: The negative tú command is different from the affirmative one. Start from the usted command (the yo form with the opposite vowel) and add -s: hablar → hable → no hables; comer → coma → no comas; escribir → escriba → no escribas. Spelling changes still apply (no busques, no pagues, no empieces). Verbs with an irregular yo form keep it (no digas, no hagas, no salgas), and five verbs have special forms.

Because attaching syllables moves the stress, a written accent is often needed: compra → cómpralo, di + me + lo → dímelo. In a negative command the pronouns stay in front of the verb and nothing is attached: no lo compres, no me lo digas.

Give me water. / Don’t give me water.

explanations.body: Vosotros is the informal “you all” of Spain. In Latin America ustedes is used for both formal and informal groups, so the vosotros commands will be heard mainly in Spain. To form the affirmative, take the infinitive and change the final -r to -d: hablar → hablad, comer → comed, escribir → escribid.

explanations.title: Drop the d before os
explanations.body: With reflexive verbs, the final -d of the vosotros command disappears when os is attached: sentad + os → sentaos, levantad + os → levantaos. With -ir verbs an accent is needed: vestid + os → vestíos. The verb ir (to go) is regular here (ir → id); the only exception is the reflexive irse, which keeps its d: idos. Other short verbs follow the regular rule: decid, haced, poned, salid, sed, tened, venid.

lessons.title: 479. Commands with vos: the voseo

explanations.title: Another “you” in Latin America
explanations.body: In Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and much of Central America, people use vos instead of tú. The affirmative command is the infinitive without its final -r, with the stress (accent) on the last vowel: hablar → hablá, comer → comé, escribir → escribí. Most verbs that are irregular for tú are regular for vos: vení, decí, hacé, poné, salí, tené (exceptions: ir → andá, ser → sé). The negative command is normally the tú form: no hables, no comas. Vos has its own present forms too (vos hablás, vos comés, vos vivís), but you only need to recognize them here.

explanations.title: Two ways to say “you” in the plural and the singular

lessons.title: 483. Review: the perfect tenses and your health

explanations.title: Present perfect and past perfect
explanations.body: The present perfect (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + participle) connects the past with now: Me he sentido mal desde ayer. The past perfect (había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían + participle) places an event before another past moment: Ya había tomado la medicina cuando llamó el médico. Remember the irregular participles: dicho, hecho, escrito, visto, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto.

When the doctor arrived, the pain had already gone.

lessons.title: 495. A rescue narrative: preterite, imperfect, por and para

explanations.title: Telling a story in the past
explanations.body: In a story, the imperfect paints the background (what was going on) and the preterite moves the plot forward (what happened). The past perfect tells what had already happened. Por and para also appear: para + infinitive for purpose (para buscar), por for means, cause, part of the day or thanks (por teléfono, por eso, por la mañana, gracias por la ayuda). Read the scene, then answer the questions.

examples.text: Una familia se quedó en el segundo piso de su casa y llamó a los bomberos por teléfono.

explanations.title: Choosing the right command under pressure
explanations.body: In an emergency the order has to be short and clear. The form depends on who is listening: usted or ustedes for strangers and groups, tú for a friend or child, vosotros in Spain, vos in Argentina or Uruguay, and nosotros for “let’s”.

lessons.title: 497. Review: the many uses of se

explanations.title: Six jobs for one little word
explanations.body: Se can mean: (1) reflexive, the subject acts on itself: Se levantó. (2) reciprocal, they act on each other: Se abrazaron. (3) a replacement for le/les before lo/la/los/las: Se lo dije. (4) impersonal, no one in particular: Se vive bien aquí. (5) passive, the thing is the subject: Se vendieron las casas. (6) accidental, it happened to someone: Se me cayó el vaso.

lessons.title: 498. Review: the present perfect and the past perfect

explanations.title: Two perfect tenses
explanations.body: Present perfect: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + participle (what has happened up to now). Past perfect: había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían + participle (what had happened before another past moment). Object pronouns go before haber: Ya los he enviado. Irregular participles: abierto, dicho, escrito, hecho, puesto, roto, visto, vuelto.

This year we have visited three countries.
We had already left when they called.

explanations.title: Future or conditional?
explanations.body: The future (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -án) states plans, predictions and guesses about the present. The conditional (-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -ían) states what would happen, polite requests and advice. They share the same irregular stems: dir-, har-, podr-, pondr-, saldr-, tendr-, vendr-, sabr-, habr-.

explanations.title: Two pairs to keep apart
explanations.body: Preterite = a finished event or a step in the story (De repente se oyó un ruido). Imperfect = a background, a habit or an action in progress (Cuando era niña, jugaba en el río). Para = purpose, recipient or deadline; por = cause, means, duration or “through”.

Terrorista can be a noun or an adjective: un terrorista, un grupo terrorista. The verbs detener (to arrest, to detain), investigar and condenar are in the news every day. Note: sembrar el terror means to spread terror.

explanations.title: Groups and agreements
explanations.body: A group that fights with weapons is un grupo armado. Una guerrilla is a group of fighters who oppose a government; a guerrillero is one of its members. Una célula is a small cell of a larger organization. Peace talks use verbs such as negociar, firmar and pactar. To stop fighting, Spanish has several equivalent expressions: el alto el fuego, el alto al fuego, el cese el fuego and el cese al fuego (a ceasefire). Una tregua is a truce.

lessons.title: 506. A new mood: the subjunctive

explanations.title: Fact or wish?
explanations.body: So far you have used the indicative (statements of fact) and the imperative (commands). The subjunctive is a third mood. It does not state a fact: it talks about wishes, hopes, doubts and feelings, things that may or may not happen. In English the idea often looks like an infinitive: Quiero que mi hijo estudie = I want my son to study.

rows: Quiero que mi hijo estudie mucho.

I want you to speak Spanish.

explanations.title: The pattern
explanations.body: A sentence with a subjunctive has two parts joined by que. The first part (the main clause) has a verb of wish, in the indicative. The second part has a different subject, and its verb is in the subjunctive.

explanations.title: Switch the vowel

exercises.promptTranslation: My mother wants you to tell her the truth.

exercises.prompt: Señora, le pido que ___ los papeles aquí.
exercises.promptTranslation: Madam, I ask you to put the papers here.

exercises.promptTranslation: I ask that you come to my house tomorrow.

exercises.promptTranslation: I need you to bring me the book.

exercises.promptTranslation: We want her to meet my brother.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct subjunctive of salir for yo?

lessons.title: 509. Stem-changing -ar and -er verbs in the subjunctive
lessons.subtitle: Quiero que cierres la puerta. Espero que vuelvan pronto.

explanations.title: Boot verbs keep their boot
explanations.body: -ar and -er verbs with a stem change in the present (e → ie, o → ue) have the same change in the subjunctive, except in the nosotros and vosotros forms, which keep the infinitive stem.

exercises.prompt: Quiero que tú ___ la puerta con llave.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to lock the door.

exercises.prompt: Mi madre espera que yo ___ pronto a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: My mother hopes that I come back home soon.

exercises.prompt: Necesitamos que ustedes ___ venir mañana.
exercises.promptTranslation: We need you to be able to come tomorrow.

exercises.prompt: El profesor quiere que nosotros ___ bien la lección.
exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher wants us to understand the lesson well.

exercises.prompt: Espero que ellos ___ la llave.
exercises.promptTranslation: I hope they find the key.

exercises.prompt: El director quiere que vosotros ___ bien antes de decidir.
exercises.promptTranslation: The director wants you to think carefully before deciding.

exercises.prompt: Te pido que no ___ tu pasaporte.
exercises.promptTranslation: I ask you not to lose your passport.

exercises.prompt: Which form of cerrar goes with nosotros in the subjunctive?
exercises.explanation: The stem does not change for nosotros.

exercises.prompt: Which is the subjunctive of poder for yo?

lessons.title: 510. Stem-changing -ir verbs in the subjunctive
lessons.subtitle: Quiero que duermas bien. Esperamos que sirvan la cena.

explanations.title: Two changes for -ir verbs
explanations.body: -ir stem-changing verbs change in the same persons as other boot verbs, but in the nosotros and vosotros forms they also change: e → i and o → u.

exercises.prompt: Mi madre quiere que yo ___ ocho horas.
exercises.promptTranslation: My mother wants me to sleep eight hours.

exercises.prompt: Te pido que ___ la pregunta, por favor.
exercises.promptTranslation: I ask you to repeat the question, please.

exercises.prompt: El jefe espera que nosotros ___ bien a los clientes.
exercises.promptTranslation: The boss hopes that we serve the customers well.

exercises.prompt: Esta noche mamá quiere que nosotros ___ temprano.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tonight Mom wants us to sleep early.

exercises.prompt: Espero que ellos no ___ a su familia.
exercises.promptTranslation: I hope they don’t lie to their family.

exercises.prompt: Quiero que ustedes ___ las instrucciones.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to follow the instructions.

exercises.prompt: Prefiero que ustedes ___ la cena en casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: I prefer that you order dinner at home.

exercises.prompt: Which form of pedir goes with nosotros in the subjunctive?
Which form of dormir goes with vosotros in the subjunctive?

lessons.title: 511. Spelling changes in the subjunctive
lessons.subtitle: busque, pague, empiece, elija

explanations.title: Keeping the sound
explanations.body: Because every -ar subjunctive ending starts with e, verbs in -car, -gar and -zar change their final consonant (c → qu, g → gu, z → c) so that the sound stays the same, in every person. Verbs in -ger and -gir already have j in the yo form (protejo, elijo), and the subjunctive keeps it: proteja, elija.

exercises.prompt: Quiero que tú ___ las llaves en la mesa.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to look for the keys on the table.

exercises.prompt: Necesitamos que alguien ___ la cuenta del hotel.
exercises.promptTranslation: We need someone to pay the hotel bill.

exercises.prompt: Mi madre espera que yo ___ a tiempo.
exercises.promptTranslation: My mother hopes that I arrive on time.

exercises.prompt: La maestra desea que nosotros ___ la clase ahora.
exercises.explanation: Empezar → empecemos (z → c; nosotros keeps e).
exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher wants us to start the class now.

exercises.prompt: Esperamos que el gobierno ___ a las víctimas.
exercises.promptTranslation: We hope that the government protects the victims.

exercises.prompt: El entrenador quiere que ustedes ___ al fútbol esta tarde.
exercises.promptTranslation: The coach wants you to play soccer this afternoon.

exercises.prompt: El jefe necesita que yo ___ un buen equipo.
exercises.promptTranslation: The boss needs me to choose a good team.

exercises.prompt: Mi papá quiere que nosotros ___ juntos hoy.
exercises.promptTranslation: My dad wants us to have lunch together today.

exercises.prompt: Why does buscar become “busque” in the subjunctive?
exercises.explanation: C before e would sound like s.

lessons.title: 512. Six irregular verbs: sea, esté, vaya, dé, sepa, haya
lessons.subtitle: Quiero que seas feliz. Espero que haya paz.

explanations.title: Learn these six by heart
explanations.body: Six verbs do not follow the yo-form rule. Note the accent on dé (to tell it apart from the preposition de) and on esté, estés, estén and estéis. Haya is the subjunctive of hay: Espero que haya paz.

exercises.prompt: Quiero que tú ___ feliz.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to be happy.

exercises.prompt: Espero que ustedes ___ bien.
exercises.promptTranslation: I hope you are well.

exercises.prompt: Mis padres quieren que yo ___ a la universidad.
exercises.promptTranslation: My parents want me to go to the university.

exercises.prompt: El maestro desea que nosotros ___ la respuesta.
exercises.promptTranslation: The teacher wants us to know the answer.

exercises.prompt: Te pido que me ___ tu número de teléfono.
exercises.promptTranslation: I ask you to give me your phone number.

exercises.prompt: Espero que ___ paz en el país.
exercises.promptTranslation: I hope there is peace in the country.

exercises.prompt: Mi madre quiere que vosotros ___ puntuales.
exercises.promptTranslation: My mother wants you to be punctual.

exercises.prompt: Mis amigos esperan que yo ___ en la fiesta.
exercises.promptTranslation: My friends hope that I will be at the party.

exercises.prompt: Why does dé have an accent?
options: Because it is in the past
To tell it apart from the preposition de

lessons.title: 513. When do we use the subjunctive? The WEDDING triggers
lessons.subtitle: Quiero que, espero que, dudo que, ojalá que…

explanations.title: A memory aid: WEDDING
explanations.body: Many teachers remember the triggers with the word WEDDING. When the first part of the sentence expresses one of these ideas, the verb after que goes in the subjunctive. In this unit you practice the first group (W: wish, will, influence); the others follow in the next units.

rows: querer que, esperar que, pedir que, recomendar que
alegrarse de que, temer que, sentir que (= to be sorry that)
dudar que, no estar seguro de que
negar que, no es verdad que
es importante que, es posible que
no creer que, no pensar que
ojalá (que), quizás, tal vez (no que; the indicative is also possible), puede que

explanations.title: Three conditions
explanations.body: For the subjunctive after a wish you need all three: (1) a trigger in the main clause (in this unit, in the present tense); (2) two different subjects; (3) the word que between the two clauses.

examples.text: Yo quiero que ustedes me ayuden con este proyecto.
examples.translation: I want you to help me with this project.

examples.text: Los profesores necesitan que los estudiantes hagan su tarea.
examples.translation: The teachers need the students to do their homework.

exercises.prompt: What does the word WEDDING help you remember?
options: The kinds of expressions that trigger the subjunctive
exercises.explanation: It is a mnemonic for the triggers.

exercises.prompt: Which main-clause verb triggers the subjunctive?
exercises.explanation: Querer is a verb of wish; saber, ver and creer (affirmative) present something as true, so they take the indicative.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence follows all three rules?
Yo quiero que ustedes me ___ con este proyecto.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to help me with this project.

exercises.prompt: Mis padres esperan ___ yo termine la carrera.
exercises.explanation: The two clauses are joined by que.
exercises.promptTranslation: My parents hope that I finish my degree.

exercises.prompt: Mi padre necesita que yo lo ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father needs me to help him.

exercises.prompt: Nosotros les aconsejamos que ___ nuestro producto.
exercises.explanation: Aconsejar que + subjunctive; les = ustedes (or ellos), so prueben.
exercises.promptTranslation: We advise you to try our product.

exercises.prompt: How many different subjects does a sentence with a wish verb + que + subjunctive need?
exercises.explanation: With wish verbs: one subject in the main clause and a different one after que. With the same subject, use the infinitive (Quiero ir).

exercises.prompt: In “Mi madre quiere que yo estudie,” which part is the subjunctive clause?

lessons.title: 514. Expressing wishes: querer, desear, esperar, anhelar
lessons.subtitle: Los padres anhelan que sus hijos vivan en paz.

explanations.title: Verbs of wish
explanations.body: These verbs express what someone wants or hopes. Anhelar and ansiar mean to long for and appear in formal speech and in the news. Esperar can also mean to wait (Espero el autobús), but with que it means to hope.

rows: Quiero que mi familia esté segura.
Los ciudadanos desean que el gobierno proteja a todos.
Esperamos que los líderes firmen la paz.
Prefieren que el diálogo empiece pronto.
El pueblo necesita que la guerra acabe.
Las familias anhelan que termine la violencia.
Ansío que mis hijos vivan sin miedo.

exercises.prompt: Las familias anhelan que la violencia ___ pronto.
exercises.promptTranslation: Families long for the violence to end soon.

exercises.prompt: Los padres ansían que sus hijos ___ en paz.
exercises.promptTranslation: Parents long for their children to live in peace.

exercises.prompt: Esperamos que los líderes ___ el acuerdo.
exercises.promptTranslation: We hope that the leaders sign the accord.

exercises.prompt: Los ciudadanos desean que el gobierno ___ a todos.
exercises.promptTranslation: The citizens want the government to protect everyone.

exercises.prompt: El pueblo necesita que la guerra ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: The people need the war to end.

exercises.prompt: Prefiero que el diálogo ___ en la capital.
exercises.promptTranslation: I prefer that the dialogue start in the capital.

exercises.prompt: Mis vecinos quieren que la policía les ___ más seguridad.
exercises.promptTranslation: My neighbors want the police to give them more security.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means “to long for”?
Which sentence means “I hope that peace comes”?

lessons.title: 515. Requests, advice and suggestions: pedir, rogar, sugerir, recomendar
lessons.subtitle: Te ruego que me escuches. Les sugiero que lean el informe.

explanations.title: Trying to influence someone
explanations.body: When you ask, beg, suggest, recommend or advise, you are trying to influence another person, so the verb after que is in the subjunctive. Notice the indirect object pronoun in the first clause: it tells you who receives the request (Te pido que…, Le sugiero que…). Insistir takes the preposition en: Insisto en que vengas.

rows: Le pido al juez que sea justo.
Les sugiero que lean el informe.
El médico recomienda que bebas agua.
Mis amigos me aconsejan que no viaje solo.
Insistimos en que el gobierno investigue.

exercises.prompt: Le pido a mi jefe que me ___ un día libre.
exercises.promptTranslation: I ask my boss to give me a day off.

exercises.prompt: Te ruego que me ___ con atención.
exercises.promptTranslation: I beg you to listen to me carefully.

exercises.prompt: Les sugiero que ___ el informe antes del lunes.
exercises.promptTranslation: I suggest that you read the report before Monday.

exercises.prompt: El médico recomienda que los pacientes ___ más agua.
exercises.promptTranslation: The doctor recommends that the patients drink more water.

exercises.prompt: Mis amigos me aconsejan que no ___ solo.
exercises.promptTranslation: My friends advise me not to travel alone.

exercises.prompt: Insistimos en que el gobierno ___ lo que pasó.
exercises.promptTranslation: We insist that the government investigate what happened.

exercises.prompt: Los expertos aconsejan que la gente no ___ información sin verificar.
exercises.explanation: Aconsejar que + subjunctive; la gente is singular.
exercises.promptTranslation: Experts advise people not to share unchecked information.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with insistir before que?
Which sentence means “I recommend that you rest”?

lessons.title: 516. Orders, permission and prohibition
lessons.subtitle: El reglamento prohíbe que los alumnos coman en clase.

explanations.title: Mandar, permitir, prohibir, exigir
explanations.body: Verbs that give orders, allow or forbid something also trigger the subjunctive: mandar que, ordenar que, permitir que, prohibir que, exigir que. After mandar, permitir and prohibir with an indirect object pronoun, an infinitive is also common: Te prohíbo que salgas = Te prohíbo salir.

rows: El alcalde manda que los vecinos limpien las calles.
La escuela permite que los estudiantes usen el teléfono.
El reglamento prohíbe que los alumnos coman en clase.
Los jueces exigen que los testigos digan la verdad.
La directora ordena que los alumnos salgan en orden.

exercises.prompt: El reglamento prohíbe que los alumnos ___ en clase.
exercises.promptTranslation: The rules forbid students to eat in class.

exercises.prompt: La escuela permite que los estudiantes ___ el teléfono en el recreo.
exercises.promptTranslation: The school allows students to use the phone at recess.

exercises.prompt: El alcalde manda que los vecinos ___ las calles.
exercises.promptTranslation: The mayor orders the neighbors to clean the streets.

exercises.prompt: Mi padre no permite que yo ___ tarde a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: My father does not allow me to arrive home late.

exercises.prompt: Los jueces exigen que los testigos ___ la verdad.
exercises.promptTranslation: The judges demand that the witnesses tell the truth.

exercises.prompt: La directora ordena que los alumnos ___ en orden.
exercises.promptTranslation: The principal orders the students to go out in an orderly way.
