exercises.promptTranslation: The mother forbids her son to go out alone.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means the same as “Te prohíbo que salgas”?
exercises.explanation: With an indirect object pronoun, the infinitive is also possible.

exercises.prompt: Which verb means “to forbid”?

lessons.title: 517. Decir que: a fact or an order?
lessons.subtitle: Mi madre dice que estudio mucho. Mi madre dice que estudie mucho.

explanations.title: One verb, two meanings
explanations.body: Decir que + indicative reports a fact: it means to say that something is true. Decir que + subjunctive tells someone what to do: it means to tell someone to do something. The same is true of other verbs of communication, such as escribir and avisar.

rows: Mi madre dice que estudio mucho.
Mi madre dice que estudie mucho.
My mother says that I study a lot. / My mother tells me to study a lot.
Petra dice que Roberto difunde las noticias.
Petra le dice a Roberto que difunda las noticias.
Petra says that Roberto spreads the news. / Petra tells Roberto to spread the news.
Mi jefe dice que llegamos temprano.
Mi jefe dice que lleguemos temprano.
My boss says that we arrive early. / My boss tells us to arrive early.

exercises.prompt: Mi madre me dice que, por favor, ___ la puerta.
exercises.promptTranslation: My mother tells me to close the door, please.

exercises.prompt: Mi hermano dice que ayer ___ al médico.
exercises.explanation: Ayer gives a past fact: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: My brother says that he went to the doctor yesterday.

exercises.prompt: El periodista dice que el gobierno ___ un nuevo plan.
exercises.explanation: A report of a fact: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: The journalist says that the government has a new plan.

exercises.prompt: La directora les dice a los alumnos que ___ en silencio, por favor.
exercises.promptTranslation: The principal tells the students to work in silence, please.

exercises.prompt: Mi amiga dice que no ___ a la fiesta porque está enferma.
exercises.explanation: Reporting a fact with a reason: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: My friend says that she is not coming to the party because she is sick.

exercises.prompt: Lupe le dice a Pedro que el gobierno ___ una tregua, pero la guerrilla sigue atacando.
exercises.explanation: A report of a fact: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: Lupe tells Pedro that the government proposes a truce, but the guerrillas keep attacking.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is an order?
options: Mi jefe dice que lleguemos temprano.
Mi jefe dijo que llegamos temprano.
Mi jefe dice que ayer llegamos temprano.
Mi jefe dice que llegamos temprano.
exercises.explanation: Subjunctive after decir = tell someone to do something.

exercises.prompt: What does “Petra le dice a Roberto que difunda la noticia” mean?
options: Petra says that Roberto spreads the news
Petra tells Roberto to spread the news

exercises.prompt: Decir que + indicative means…
options: to tell someone to do something
to say that something is true
exercises.explanation: Decir que + indicative reports a fact.

lessons.title: 518. Same subject? Use the infinitive
lessons.subtitle: Quiero hablar español. Quiero que tú hables español.

explanations.title: One subject: infinitive. Two subjects: que + subjunctive
explanations.body: When the person who wants and the person who acts are the same, Spanish uses the infinitive. When they are different, it uses que and the subjunctive.

rows: I want to speak Spanish. / I want you to speak Spanish.
Espero que ellos lleguen a tiempo.
I hope to arrive on time. / I hope they arrive on time.
Mi esposa prefiere comprar una casa.
Yo prefiero que nosotros compremos una casa.
My wife prefers to buy a house. / I prefer that we buy a house.

exercises.prompt: Yo quiero ___ español en Chile.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want to speak Spanish in Chile.

exercises.prompt: Yo quiero que tú ___ español en Chile.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want you to speak Spanish in Chile.

exercises.prompt: Mis padres esperan ___ a Monterey el próximo mes.
exercises.explanation: The parents are the subject of both verbs: infinitive.
exercises.promptTranslation: My parents hope to come to Monterey next month.

exercises.prompt: Mis padres esperan que yo ___ a Monterey el próximo mes.
exercises.promptTranslation: My parents hope that I will go to Monterey next month.

exercises.prompt: Necesito ___ mi coche hoy.
exercises.promptTranslation: I need to fix my car today.

exercises.prompt: Necesito que mi hermano me ___ con el coche.
exercises.promptTranslation: I need my brother to help me with the car.

exercises.prompt: Mi esposa prefiere ___ una casa en el norte.
exercises.promptTranslation: My wife prefers to buy a house in the north.

exercises.prompt: Yo prefiero que nosotros ___ una casa en el sur.
exercises.promptTranslation: I prefer that we buy a house in the south.

exercises.prompt: When both clauses have the same subject, Spanish uses…

lessons.title: 519. Pronouns with the subjunctive
lessons.subtitle: Quiero que me llames. Espero que te lo den.

explanations.title: Same rules as in the indicative
explanations.body: Object pronouns go before a conjugated subjunctive verb. They are not attached to it (attaching is only for affirmative commands, infinitives and gerunds). With two verbs, the pronoun goes before the first conjugated verb or after the infinitive. Remember le/les becomes se before lo, la, los, las.

examples.translation: I want my parents to buy me a new car.

examples.text: Espero que nos ayuden con el proyecto.
examples.translation: I hope they help us with the project.

examples.translation: I hope my parents come to visit me.

exercises.prompt: Quiero que mis padres me ___ un coche nuevo.

exercises.promptTranslation: I hope you call me soon.

exercises.explanation: Se la before the subjunctive verb.
exercises.promptTranslation: The letter is important: I want you to deliver it to her today.

exercises.prompt: Espero que mis padres me ___ a visitar.
exercises.explanation: Venir a + infinitive in the subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I hope my parents come to visit me.

exercises.prompt: Es un secreto: no quiero que nadie se lo ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: It is a secret: I don’t want anyone to tell it to him.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explanation: The pronoun goes before the subjunctive verb.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Espero que mis padres vengan a visitarme.
Espero que mis padres vengan me a visitar.
Espero que mis padres me visitarvengan.
Espero que mis padres venganme a visitar.

lessons.title: 520. Reading: Peru, Sendero Luminoso and a reader’s letter
lessons.subtitle: Espero que las autoridades protejan a las víctimas.

explanations.title: Background and a letter to the editor
explanations.body: Between 1980 and 2000, Peru lived through an internal armed conflict. The group Sendero Luminoso (Shining Path) began its armed struggle in 1980. The text below gives the facts in the indicative and then the writer’s wishes in the subjunctive.

examples.text: Entre mil novecientos ochenta y el año dos mil, Perú vivió un conflicto armado interno.
examples.translation: Between 1980 and 2000 Peru lived through an internal armed conflict.

examples.text: El grupo Sendero Luminoso empezó la lucha armada en mil novecientos ochenta.
examples.translation: The group Sendero Luminoso began the armed struggle in 1980.

examples.text: Según la Comisión de la Verdad, murieron unas sesenta y nueve mil personas.
examples.translation: According to the Truth Commission, about 69,000 people died.

examples.text: Su fundador, Abimael Guzmán, fue capturado en mil novecientos noventa y dos y murió en prisión en dos mil veintiuno.
examples.translation: Its founder, Abimael Guzmán, was captured in 1992 and died in prison in 2021.

examples.text: Señor director: espero que las autoridades estén atentas y que protejan a las víctimas.
examples.translation: To the editor: I hope the authorities stay alert and protect the victims.

examples.text: Prefiero que las leyes sean claras y justas, y ruego que haya una paz duradera.
examples.translation: I prefer that the laws be clear and fair, and I beg that there be a lasting peace.

examples.text: También sugiero que los jóvenes conozcan la historia de su país.
examples.translation: I also suggest that young people know the history of their country.

exercises.prompt: What happened in Peru between 1980 and 2000?
Who was Abimael Guzmán?
options: A judge of the Truth Commission

exercises.prompt: About how many people died, according to the Truth Commission?
Where did Guzmán die?
Señor director: espero que las autoridades ___ atentas.
exercises.promptTranslation: To the editor: I hope the authorities stay alert.

exercises.prompt: Pido que el gobierno ___ a las víctimas.
exercises.promptTranslation: I ask that the government protect the victims.

exercises.prompt: Ruego que ___ una paz duradera.
exercises.promptTranslation: I beg that there be a lasting peace.

exercises.prompt: Sugiero que los jóvenes ___ la historia de su país.
exercises.promptTranslation: I suggest that young people know the history of their country.

exercises.prompt: Entre mil novecientos ochenta y el año dos mil, Perú ___ un conflicto armado.
exercises.explanation: Finished period in the past: preterite.
exercises.promptTranslation: Between 1980 and 2000, Peru lived through an armed conflict.

lessons.title: 521. Reading: the attacks in Barcelona and Cambrils, 2017
lessons.subtitle: El diecisiete de agosto de dos mil diecisiete ocurrió un atentado en La Rambla.

explanations.title: A news report
explanations.body: This report uses the preterite for events in order. Useful new words: la furgoneta (van), el peatón (pedestrian), atropellar (to run over), huir (to flee). Notice how the report names the facts without giving the attackers a heroic image: the focus is on the victims and the city’s response.

examples.text: El diecisiete de agosto de dos mil diecisiete ocurrió un atentado en La Rambla, una calle famosa de Barcelona.
examples.translation: On August 17, 2017 an attack took place on La Rambla, a famous street in Barcelona.

examples.text: Un conductor atropelló a muchos peatones con una furgoneta.
examples.translation: A driver ran over many pedestrians with a van.

examples.text: Horas después hubo otro ataque en Cambrils, una ciudad de la costa.
examples.translation: Hours later there was another attack in Cambrils, a coastal city.

examples.text: Murieron personas de muchos países y más de cien personas resultaron heridas.
examples.translation: People from many countries died and more than a hundred people were injured.

examples.text: Días después la policía encontró al conductor de la furgoneta.
examples.translation: Days later the police found the driver of the van.

examples.text: El grupo Estado Islámico dijo que era responsable del atentado.
examples.translation: The Islamic State group said it was responsible for the attack.

examples.text: Los líderes de España y de Cataluña condenaron los ataques.
examples.translation: The leaders of Spain and Catalonia condemned the attacks.

examples.text: Miles de personas se reunieron en una plaza para rechazar el odio.

explanations.body: Spanish has many interjections to react to shocking news. Their strength and regional flavor vary: ¡caramba! (wow, darn), ¡chale! (Mexico: no way), ¡púchica! and ¡pucha! (Central America, Chile: darn), ¡Dios mío!, ¡qué horror!, ¡qué barbaridad!, ¡qué pena! and ¡no lo puedo creer!. Spanish also has much stronger, vulgar interjections whose meaning changes with the region and the tone. You will hear them, but avoid using them until you know the setting well.

lessons.title: 525. Review: forming the present subjunctive

explanations.title: Summary
explanations.body: 1) Start from the yo form of the present. 2) Drop -o and add the “opposite” vowel: -e endings for -ar verbs, -a endings for -er and -ir verbs. 3) Keep irregular yo stems (tengo → tenga, conozco → conozca). 4) Boot verbs: -ar and -er keep the infinitive stem in nosotros and vosotros; -ir verbs change e→i or o→u there. 5) Spelling changes keep the sound or follow spelling rules (busque, pague, llegue; z → c: empiece). 6) Six irregulars: sea, esté, vaya, dé, sepa, haya.

explanations.title: One more look at the triggers
explanations.body: Wish: querer, desear, esperar, preferir, necesitar, anhelar, ansiar. Influence: pedir, rogar, sugerir, recomendar, aconsejar, insistir en, decir (to tell someone to). Orders and permission: mandar, ordenar, permitir, prohibir, exigir. Two subjects → usually que + subjunctive (with permitir, prohibir, mandar and aconsejar an infinitive is also common: Te prohíbo salir). One subject → infinitive. A fact → indicative.

lessons.title: 527. Review: indicative, subjunctive or infinitive?

explanations.title: Three questions to ask
explanations.body: 1) Is the first verb a trigger (wish, request, order, emotion, doubt, denial, or an impersonal expression such as es necesario que)? If not, it usually states, reports or affirms something (saber que, ver que, and belief verbs such as creer que): use the indicative. 2) If it is a trigger, are there two different subjects? Then que + subjunctive. 3) If there is only one subject, usually use the infinitive (Quiero vivir en Lima). With doubt and denial, que + subjunctive is common even with one subject (No creo que pueda ir).

lessons.title: 534. Reading: four short reports about drug seizures (practice texts)

explanations.title: Practice reading: invented reports
explanations.body: These four items are invented practice texts in the style of agency reports. They use the passive voice (fue detenido) and the preterite. Useful words: asegurar (here, to seize), desmantelar (to dismantle), la red (network), la lancha (boat), interceptar.

explanations.title: How Mexico’s modern cartels began
explanations.body: The first large Mexican drug organization is usually said to be the Guadalajara cartel. The text below uses se + verb to say what happened without naming who did it (se formó), and the preterite passive (fue detenido).

examples.text: A Félix Gallardo lo conocían como el jefe de jefes.
examples.translation: People knew Félix Gallardo as the boss of bosses.

explanations.title: A policy and a debate

explanations.body: El Triángulo Norte is the name for El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras. Two gangs became famous there: the Mara Salvatrucha (MS-13) and Barrio 18. Both were born in Los Angeles. The text uses the imperfect for what used to happen and the preterite for events.

explanations.title: Press freedom
explanations.body: La libertad de prensa is the freedom of journalists to report. La impunidad means that crimes are not punished. In some regions, reporting on organized crime is dangerous. Press organizations ask governments to protect journalists and investigate every case.

lessons.title: 540. Emotions and the subjunctive: me alegro de que…
lessons.subtitle: Me alegro de que estés aquí. Siento que no puedas venir.

explanations.title: Feelings about what someone else does
explanations.body: When you express an emotion about something another person does or is, the verb after que goes in the subjunctive. The emotion is the trigger (the E in WEDDING). Sentir que and lamentar que mean to be sorry that. Note the preposition de: alegrarse de que, estar contento de que, tener miedo de que.

rows: Me alegro de que estés aquí.
Estamos contentos de que ustedes vengan.
Estoy triste de que mi amigo se vaya.
Temo que el viaje sea peligroso.
Tengo miedo de que llegue tarde.

explanations.title: The same three conditions
explanations.body: As with wishes: (1) an emotion in the main clause, (2) two different subjects, (3) que between the clauses. In Siento que estés triste, sentir means to be sorry. Siento frío is a different use: I feel cold.

examples.text: Mi madre se alegra de que yo apruebe el examen.

examples.text: Lamento que tu abuelo esté enfermo.
examples.translation: I am sorry that your grandfather is sick.

explanations.title: Fear and anger
explanations.body: Fear and anger are emotions too, so they trigger the subjunctive when the subject changes. Temer que and tener miedo de que express fear. For anger, Spanish often uses Me enoja que… or Me enfada que… (it makes me angry that…), and enojarse de que is also heard. In Mexico and Central America enojarse is more common than enfadarse.

explanations.title: One subject or two?
explanations.body: With emotions the rule is the same as with wishes. If the feeling and the action belong to the same person, use the infinitive. If they belong to different people, use que + subjunctive.

Me alegro de que estés aquí conmigo.

explanations.title: A hidden “I wish”
explanations.body: Many everyday wishes start with que and a subjunctive verb. The first part (Deseo que… / Quiero que…) is understood but not said. Use the tú form with friends and the usted form for someone you address formally.

rows: Have a good time! (to a group)
May it go well for you!

lessons.title: 545. Ojalá (que): I hope so!
lessons.subtitle: Ojalá que mañana haga buen tiempo. ¡Ojalá que sí!

explanations.title: Ojalá
explanations.body: Ojalá expresses a strong wish and always takes the subjunctive. Que is optional: Ojalá llueva and Ojalá que llueva are both correct. The word comes from Arabic, from an expression meaning “if God wills” (law shāʾ Allāh), and it entered Spanish in the Middle Ages. It never changes form. To answer a question you can say ¡Ojalá que sí! (I hope so) or ¡Ojalá que no! (I hope not).

rows: Ojalá que mañana haga buen tiempo.
I hope the weather is good tomorrow.
Ojalá que no llueva el sábado.
I hope it does not rain on Saturday.

lessons.title: 546. Probability: tal vez, quizás, puede que

explanations.title: Maybe…
explanations.body: To say that something is possible but not certain, use tal vez, quizá or quizás, or puede que (also puede ser que). These expressions of probability are followed by the subjunctive. Some speakers use the indicative after tal vez and quizás when they feel almost sure, but this course practices the subjunctive. Puede que always takes the subjunctive. The exception is a lo mejor (maybe), which takes the indicative.

lessons.title: 547. Talking about the future: three tools

explanations.title: Three ways to look ahead
explanations.body: 1) ir a + infinitive: a plan or a near future (Mañana voy a visitar a mis abuelos). 2) The future tense: a prediction or a promise (Te prometo que te llamaré). 3) The present subjunctive: after a wish, an emotion or an expression of doubt or probability, the present subjunctive often points to the future (Espero que me llames mañana; Quizás llueva el domingo). The trigger decides: a fact or plan uses the indicative or the future; a wish, a feeling or a doubt uses the subjunctive.

lessons.title: 557. SOUTHCOM: the U.S. Southern Command
lessons.subtitle: El Comando Sur coopera con muchos países de América Latina.

explanations.title: Who and where
explanations.body: The Comando Sur de los Estados Unidos (SOUTHCOM) is one of the regional commands of the U.S. armed forces. Its area of responsibility includes Central America, South America and most of the Caribbean. Mexico belongs to a different regional command, the Comando Norte. Today its headquarters is in Florida; until 1997 it was in Panama.

examples.text: El Comando Sur de los Estados Unidos, o SOUTHCOM, es uno de los comandos regionales de las fuerzas armadas estadounidenses.

explanations.title: What it does today
explanations.body: SOUTHCOM describes its work as helping with humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, working with the armed forces and police of partner countries, and supporting efforts against drug trafficking and other kinds of crime. Some governments and critics in the region disagree about how large a role the U.S. military should have; that debate is part of Latin American politics.

lessons.title: 558. Reading: the School of the Americas, a timeline

explanations.title: From Panama to Georgia
explanations.body: The School of the Americas (Escuela de las Américas) was a U.S. Army training school for Latin American military personnel. This timeline follows the school's history.

explanations.title: A long debate
explanations.body: The school has been the subject of a long public debate in the United States and Latin America. This reading reports what each side says, with attributed sources.

lessons.title: 560. Plan Colombia: the three phases
lessons.subtitle: El Plan Colombia fue un programa de cooperación entre Colombia y los Estados Unidos.

explanations.title: A program in three phases
explanations.body: The Plan Colombia was a program of cooperation between Colombia and the United States. Its U.S. support was concentrated from the end of the 1990s to about 2012, and it combined security aid with institutional reconstruction. Analysts usually divide it into phases. In Spanish, mil millones = a billion (un billón = a trillion, 10^12).

rows: mil novecientos noventa y ocho a dos mil dos
Proceso de paz y reforma de las fuerzas militares
dos mil dos a dos mil seis
Lucha contra la insurgencia y desmovilización de los grupos paramilitares
dos mil seis a dos mil doce
Consolidar resultados y fortalecer instituciones civiles

explanations.title: Reading the phases
explanations.body: Colombia had become the leading cocaine producer in the world, and armed groups had grown stronger in the 1990s. According to one report, the United States sent about ten billion dollars (diez mil millones) between 2000 and 2016. The plan was not only a military strategy: it also supported courts, police, alternative crops and other civilian programs.

examples.translation: According to a report, the United States sent about ten billion dollars between 2000 and 2016.

examples.translation: In the second phase, the focus was the fight against insurgency and the demobilization of paramilitary groups.

examples.text: En la tercera fase se trabajó para fortalecer también las instituciones civiles.
examples.translation: In the third phase, work was done to strengthen civilian institutions as well.

lessons.title: 561. Plan Colombia: success or failure?
lessons.subtitle: Para unos fue un éxito; para otros, un fracaso.

explanations.title: Two evaluations
explanations.body: Experts still disagree about the results. A 2020 report by a U.S. drug-policy commission concluded that the plan helped Colombia, which had been close to becoming a “failed state,” to succeed against the insurgency, but that it failed in its drug-control goals. Other analysts add that coca cultivation went down in some years and up in others, and that some programs, such as aerial spraying, hurt farmers and caused debate.

explanations.body: In the 1980s General Manuel Noriega, head of the Panamanian Defense Forces, was Panama's de facto ruler. This reading summarizes the main facts and the two views of the 1989 U.S. intervention. It does not describe military operations.

explanations.title: Expressions
explanations.body: Some everyday expressions began in military life or in historical battles. Learn them as whole phrases: you cannot translate them word by word.

meterse en camisa de once varas

no hay moros en la costa
No hay moros en la costa. Podemos hablar ahora.

for all hell to break loose

caer como un balde de agua fría
to come as a cold shock

explanations.title: Origins and notes
explanations.body: Estribos are stirrups: a rider who loses them loses control. San Quintín refers to a famous battle of 1557. The Moors in no hay moros en la costa recall the watch for raiders along the coast in past centuries. Caer como un balde de agua fría expresses a sudden surprise or disappointment, and the verb caer agrees with the thing that arrives.

explanations.title: Direct objects and their pronouns
explanations.body: The direct object answers the question What? or Whom? (¿Qué llevan? El agua. ¿A quién ven? A la víctima.). The pronoun replaces the noun and agrees with it in gender and number.

explanations.title: Where does the pronoun go?
explanations.body: Before a conjugated verb: La llevan. With two verbs, before the first one or attached to the infinitive: Lo voy a llamar = Voy a llamarlo. With affirmative commands it is attached (Ciérrala) and with negative commands it stays before the verb (No la cierres).

explanations.title: Indirect objects
explanations.body: The indirect object answers To whom? or For whom? (¿A quién le dan agua? A los damnificados.). The pronouns are me, te, le, nos, os, les. Le and les do not show gender. Spanish usually repeats the person: the pronoun is used even when a noun with a is also present.

explanations.title: The order and the change to se
explanations.body: When both pronouns appear, the indirect pronoun always comes first: me lo, te lo, nos lo… Le and les become se before lo, la, los, las: Le doy el informe → Se lo doy. Se tells you nothing about who or how many, so context or a phrase with a clarifies it (a ella, a ustedes).

Les digo la noticia a mis padres.

explanations.title: Position
explanations.body: Both pronouns move together: Se lo voy a explicar = Voy a explicárselo. In affirmative commands they attach (Dámelo) and an accent may be needed; in negative commands they stay before the verb (No se lo digas).

lessons.title: 571. Verbs that work like gustar: preocupar, sorprender, molestar…
lessons.subtitle: Al gobierno le preocupa la inestabilidad del país.

explanations.title: Like gustar
explanations.body: Gustar does not literally mean to like: it means to be pleasing. The thing that causes the feeling is the subject, and the person who feels it is the indirect object. Many verbs of feeling work the same way. The verb agrees with the thing (singular or plural), and the pronoun shows the person.

rows: to sadden (in Mexico often: to embarrass)
Al gobierno le apena la inestabilidad del país.
A los estudiantes les emocionan las vacaciones.
to surprise, to seem strange (in Latin America extrañar usually means “to miss”: Te extraño)
Al líder le indignan las mentiras.
Al ministro le preocupan los disturbios.
A los ciudadanos les molesta el ruido.
Me encantan los libros de historia.

explanations.title: How it works
explanations.body: Order: (a + person) + pronoun + verb + thing. A mí me preocupa el precio. A ellos les preocupan los precios. The a + person phrase is optional but common; the pronoun is never optional.

explanations.title: Two choices every time
explanations.body: With these verbs you make two choices: (1) the pronoun, which shows who feels (me, te, le, nos, os, les), and (2) the verb ending, which is almost always third person singular or plural to agree with the thing (-a/-an for -ar verbs such as preocupa/preocupan, -e/-en for -er verbs such as sorprende/sorprenden). The extra phrase a mí, a ti, a él, a nosotros… is for emphasis or clarity.

lessons.title: 579. Review: direct and indirect object pronouns
lessons.subtitle: Se lo doy. Te la mando. Dímelo.

explanations.title: Summary
explanations.body: Direct object: me, te, lo, la, nos, os, los, las (what? whom?). Indirect object: me, te, le, nos, os, les (to whom?). Together: indirect first (me lo, te la, nos los) and le/les become se (se lo, se la). Position: before a conjugated verb; with an infinitive, either attached or before the conjugated verb (voy a dárselo / se lo voy a dar); attached to an affirmative command; before a negative command.

examples.text: Le entrego el informe al director. Se lo entrego hoy.

explanations.title: How does a word enter the dictionary?

If no Spanish word has succeeded, they may accept the loanword. Many technology words have been added.

explanations.title: Two layers
explanations.body: The surface web (la internet superficial) is what search engines show. The deep web (la internet profunda) is everything else that is not indexed: your email, your bank account, private databases. Most of it is ordinary and legal. A small part, sometimes called la web oscura, needs special software that hides the user's identity. Privacy tools can protect journalists and activists, but criminals also use them, and that makes police work harder.

explanations.title: Money without coins
explanations.body: Cryptocurrencies (criptomonedas or criptodivisas) exist only on the network. They have no physical form and no central bank behind them. Some people like them because transfers can be quick and need no bank. Critics point to risks: prices can change a lot, scams exist, and criminals can use them to demand ransoms, launder money or evade taxes. Governments debate how to regulate them.

explanations.title: What is a tax haven?
explanations.body: A paraíso fiscal is a territory that charges foreign people and companies little or no tax and usually shares little financial information with other countries' tax authorities. A sociedad offshore is a company registered in a country where it does no business. Having one is not always illegal. It becomes a crime when the owner hides the money from the tax authorities of his or her home country (evasión fiscal).

lessons.title: 592. Leaks and whistleblowers: Panama Papers and Pandora Papers
lessons.subtitle: Los periodistas publicaron millones de documentos sobre empresas en el extranjero.

explanations.title: Big leaks
explanations.body: A filtración is a leak: secret documents given to journalists. A denunciante is a person who reports wrongdoing; the English word is whistleblower. (Informante usually means an informant or a source.) The Panama Papers, published in 2016, came from the files of a Panamanian law firm. In 2021 the Pandora Papers, about twelve million files, came from several firms that create offshore companies. International teams of journalists studied them. The documents showed that politicians, businesspeople and other well-known people owned offshore companies. Owning one is not automatically a crime, and several people named said they broke no law.

lessons.title: 594. Money laundering: lavado de dinero

explanations.title: Making dirty money look clean
explanations.body: Lavado de dinero (or lavado de activos) means hiding the illegal origin of money so that it looks legitimate. The crime that produced the money may be drug trafficking, corruption or fraud. It harms society because it lets criminals enjoy their profits and weakens honest businesses. Banks and other companies must report suspicious operations to the authorities.

lessons.title: 595. Human trafficking: trata de personas
lessons.subtitle: La trata de personas afecta a mujeres, hombres, niñas y niños.

explanations.title: What it is
explanations.body: La trata de personas (human trafficking) means recruiting, moving or holding people by force, threats or deceit in order to exploit them, for example in forced labor or sexual exploitation. The older expression trata de blancas is now considered inaccurate because trafficking affects people of every background, women, men and children. It is different from el tráfico de migrantes (smuggling), where people pay to be taken across a border, although smuggling can become trafficking.

explanations.title: Not sure, so subjunctive

The doubt can be about a different subject or the same one. Dudar que and no estar seguro de que are the two basic expressions. When you are sure, use the indicative: Estoy seguro de que llegarán a tiempo.

explanations.title: Denying a statement
explanations.body: When you deny that something is true, the verb in the que clause is in the subjunctive. Negar que is the main verb of denial. Es cierto que and es verdad que state a fact (indicative), but their negatives, no es cierto que and no es verdad que, deny it (subjunctive). Es falso que also takes the subjunctive. If the subject stays the same, the infinitive is common: Sergio niega haber robado.

explanations.title: A long debate
explanations.body: Extradition (la extradición) is the handing over of a person to another country to be tried or to serve a sentence. In Colombia it became a central issue in the fight against drug trafficking. This reading summarizes the main facts and the two sides of the debate.

lessons.title: 616. Reading: anonymity, hacktivists and the debate about privacy
lessons.subtitle: El anonimato protege la privacidad, pero también puede esconder delitos.

explanations.title: Two edges
explanations.body: Anonymity on the Internet is a double-edged tool. It protects privacy and free expression, especially for people living under repressive governments. It can also hide harassment, fraud and other crimes. Anonymous is the name of a loose online movement of hacktivists with no formal leaders. It has been praised by supporters and criticized by governments, companies and some observers. Some of its members were arrested and prosecuted in several countries.

examples.translation: At the same time, companies and governments gather a lot of information about users.

examples.translation: Several members were arrested, and some received sentences.

examples.translation: Many experts think that movements like this will appear again in the future, under other names.

explanations.title: Three questions
explanations.body: 1) Is the main verb a wish, request, order or advice? 2) Do the two clauses have different subjects? Then que + subjunctive. 3) Same subject? Then the infinitive. lessons.title: 623. Which form? Indicative, subjunctive, infinitive or future

explanations.title: A checklist
explanations.body: 1) Does the main clause state a fact, belief or certainty (sé que, creo que, veo que, estoy seguro de que, es verdad que)? → indicative or future. 2) Does it express a wish, emotion, doubt, denial, value judgment (es bueno que, es importante que), probability or order, and are the subjects different? → subjunctive. 3) Same subject? → infinitive. 4) Plain prediction or promise? → future tense.

lessons.title: 633. Review: formal commands (usted, ustedes) at a public office

explanations.title: Formal commands: a quick review
explanations.body: Take the yo form of the present, drop the -o and add the “opposite” vowel: -ar verbs take -e / -en, and -er / -ir verbs take -a / -an. Five verbs are irregular: dar → dé, estar → esté, ir → vaya, saber → sepa, ser → sea. To say “don’t”, put no before the command.

lessons.title: 634. Review: informal commands (tú) with eight irregular verbs

explanations.title: Tú commands: a quick review
explanations.body: A regular affirmative tú command looks like the él form of the present: habla, come, escribe. Eight verbs have special affirmative forms. For the negative, use the “opposite vowel” (subjunctive) form of tú: no hables, no comas, no escribas.

lessons.title: 635. Commands with pronouns: dígame, no me lo diga, dígaselo

explanations.title: Where the pronouns go
explanations.body: With an affirmative command, the pronouns attach to the end of the verb and the written accent keeps the stress where it was: diga → dígame. With a negative command, the pronouns stay in front of the verb and nothing is attached: no me diga. When two pronouns appear, the indirect one comes first (me, te, nos, se) and then lo, la, los, las. Le and les become se before lo, la, los, las.

rows: Tell it to him, her or them
tables.note: Pronouns attach in the affirmative and stay apart in the negative.

lessons.title: 636. Reading: a health center poster

explanations.title: A notice in a waiting room

lessons.title: 637. A noun and a clause: when to use the subjunctive after que
lessons.subtitle: Busco un médico que hable español. Conozco a un médico que habla español.

explanations.title: Adjectival clauses
explanations.body: A clause that describes a noun is an adjectival clause: un médico que habla español. If you are talking about someone or something that you know exists, use the indicative. If you are looking for or wishing for something whose existence is uncertain or unknown, use the present subjunctive.

rows: Tengo un médico que habla español.
Busco un médico que hable español.
Vivo en una casa que tiene tres cuartos.
Quiero una casa que tenga tres cuartos.
Hay un trabajo que paga bien.
Necesito un trabajo que pague bien.
tables.note: The speaker’s knowledge decides the mood, not the verb in the first clause.

explanations.title: Clues in the sentence
explanations.body: Look for words that show that the speaker does not know whether the thing exists: busco, necesito, quiero, prefiero, ¿hay algo que…?

examples.text: Necesito un trabajo que pague mejor que el actual.
examples.translation: I need a job that pays better than my current one.

examples.text: Tengo un trabajo que paga muy bien.
examples.translation: I have a job that pays very well.

examples.text: Buscamos una escuela que esté cerca de nuestro barrio.
examples.translation: We are looking for a school that is near our neighborhood.

examples.text: Mis hijos van a una escuela que está cerca de nuestro barrio.
examples.translation: My children go to a school that is near our neighborhood.

exercises.prompt: Busco un médico que ___ español; todavía no sé si hay alguno en el pueblo.
exercises.explanation: The doctor may not exist: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am looking for a doctor who speaks Spanish; I don’t know yet whether there is one in town.

exercises.prompt: Tengo un médico que ___ español; se llama doctor Rivas.
exercises.explanation: A specific doctor who exists: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I have a doctor who speaks Spanish; his name is Dr. Rivas.

exercises.prompt: Necesito un trabajo que ___ mejor; el actual paga muy poco.
exercises.explanation: A job I don’t have yet: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I need a job that pays better; my current one pays very little.

exercises.prompt: Trabajo en una fábrica que ___ cerca de mi casa.
exercises.explanation: A specific factory that exists: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: I work in a factory that is near my house.

exercises.prompt: Quiero una casa que ___ tres cuartos; todavía estoy buscando.
exercises.explanation: A house I have not found yet: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want a house that has three bedrooms; I’m still looking.

exercises.prompt: En mi barrio hay una clínica pública que ___ gratis a los niños.
exercises.explanation: I am stating that it exists: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: In my neighborhood there is a public clinic that treats children for free.

Voy a una escuela que ofrece clases gratis.
Hay una escuela que ofrece clases gratis.
Conozco una escuela que ofrece clases gratis.
exercises.explanation: Only the search for something that may not exist uses the subjunctive (ofrezca).

exercises.prompt: Why does “Tengo un amigo que trabaja allí” use the indicative?
options: The friend exists and the speaker knows him

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between “Busco un libro que explica la crisis” and “Busco un libro que explique la crisis”?

There is no difference at all

lessons.title: 638. Nothing and nobody: no hay nadie que…, no conozco ningún… que…
lessons.subtitle: No hay nadie que pueda ayudarnos. No conozco ninguna escuela que sea gratis.

explanations.title: When the thing does not exist
explanations.body: If the main clause says that nobody or nothing of that kind exists (no hay nadie que…, no conozco ningún… que…), the noun in the que clause does not exist for the speaker, so use the subjunctive. Before a masculine singular noun, alguno and ninguno become algún and ningún: algún trabajo, ningún lugar.

rows: No hay nadie que me ayude.
Conozco una escuela que es gratis.
No conozco ninguna escuela que sea gratis.
Tengo un amigo que vive aquí.
No tengo ningún amigo que viva aquí.
No hay nada que pueda hacer.

explanations.title: Typical sentences
explanations.body: These sentences often appear in debates about services that are missing.

examples.text: En este pueblo no hay ningún hospital que tenga un especialista.
examples.translation: In this town there is no hospital that has a specialist.

examples.text: No hay nadie que quiera trabajar por un sueldo tan bajo.

examples.text: No conozco ningún lugar que sea barato en esta ciudad.

exercises.promptTranslation: In this town there is nobody who can help us with the documents.

exercises.prompt: No conozco ninguna escuela que ___ gratis en este barrio.
exercises.explanation: No such school exists for me: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: I don’t know any school that is free in this neighborhood.

exercises.prompt: Hay una escuela que ___ gratis en el barrio vecino; la conozco bien.
exercises.explanation: It exists and I know it: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: There is a school that is free in the next neighborhood; I know it well.

exercises.prompt: No tengo ningún amigo que ___ en esta ciudad.
exercises.promptTranslation: I don’t have any friend who lives in this city.

exercises.prompt: No hay nada que nosotros ___ hacer hoy.
exercises.explanation: Nothing exists that we can do: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: There is nothing that we can do today.

exercises.prompt: En la ciudad hay algo que me ___ mucho: el transporte público.
exercises.explanation: The thing exists and I am naming it: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: In the city there is something that worries me a lot: public transportation.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says that no such hospital exists?
options: Hay un hospital que atiende a niños en este pueblo.
Conozco un hospital que atiende a niños.
Hay hospitales que atienden a niños.
No hay ningún hospital que atienda a niños en este pueblo.
exercises.explanation: Only the sentence with “no hay ningún … que” denies existence.

exercises.prompt: What happens to “ninguno” before a masculine singular noun?
Which is correct?
options: No hay nadie que sabiendo la respuesta.
No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta.
No hay nadie que saber la respuesta.
No hay nadie que sabe la respuesta.

lessons.title: 639. Asking about people and things: ¿hay alguien que…? and the personal a
lessons.subtitle: ¿Hay alguien que hable ruso? ¿Conoces a alguien que sepa de leyes?

explanations.title: Questions with alguien and algo
explanations.body: When you ask about something whose existence you do not know, the question uses the subjunctive: ¿Hay alguien que hable ruso? If the speaker already knows that such a person exists, the indicative is used: Hay alguien que habla ruso en la oficina.

rows: Is there anyone who speaks Russian?
¿Conoces a alguien que sepa de leyes?
Do you know anyone who knows about law?
Is there any interpreter who works here?
Do you need someone to help you?

explanations.title: The personal a
explanations.body: Spanish puts a before a direct object that is a specific person, and always before alguien, nadie, alguno and ninguno when they refer to people. It is not used with hay or tener in the basic meaning, and it is generally left out with an unspecified person after necesitar or buscar when the noun is introduced by un or una.

examples.text: Busco a alguien que me explique este trámite.
examples.translation: I am looking for someone who can explain this procedure to me.

examples.text: No conozco a nadie que trabaje en ese ministerio.
examples.translation: I don’t know anybody who works in that ministry.

examples.text: ¿Conoces a alguien que tenga un coche?
examples.translation: Do you know someone who has a car?

examples.text: Conozco a una abogada que atiende a personas sin dinero.
examples.translation: I know a lawyer who helps people without money.

exercises.prompt: ¿Hay alguien en esta oficina que ___ ruso? Necesitamos ayuda.
exercises.explanation: You do not know whether such a person exists: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Is there anyone in this office who speaks Russian? We need help.

exercises.prompt: En esa oficina hay una señora que ___ ruso; ya hablé con ella.
exercises.explanation: She exists and you know her: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: In that office there is a lady who speaks Russian; I have already spoken with her.

exercises.prompt: ¿Conoces a alguien que ___ de leyes?
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you know anyone who knows about law?

exercises.prompt: No conozco ___ nadie que trabaje en ese ministerio.
exercises.promptTranslation: I don’t know anybody who works in that ministry.

exercises.prompt: Busco ___ alguien que me explique este trámite.
exercises.promptTranslation: I am looking for someone who can explain this procedure to me.

exercises.prompt: ¿Necesitas a alguien que te ___ con la tarea?
exercises.promptTranslation: Do you need someone to help you with the homework?

exercises.prompt: Which question assumes that the person may not exist?
options: ¿Quién es la persona que traduce los documentos?
¿Hay alguien que traduce documentos en la oficina de la esquina?
¿Dónde está la señora que traduce documentos?
exercises.explanation: Only the question with “traduzca” is in the subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence needs the personal a?
options: Conozco ___ la directora de la escuela.
Tengo ___ tres sillas en mi casa.
exercises.explanation: A before a specific person (la directora).

exercises.prompt: What does “No conozco a nadie que sepa la respuesta” mean?
options: I know everyone who knows the answer
I don’t know anyone who knows the answer
exercises.explanation: Nadie + subjunctive = nobody of that kind.

lessons.title: 640. Anyone who…, whatever…: cualquiera, quien, los que, lo que
lessons.subtitle: Quien quiera ayudar puede inscribirse. Haz lo que puedas.

explanations.title: Open groups with the subjunctive
explanations.body: When you refer to an open, unknown group (anyone who…, whoever…, whatever…), the subjunctive follows. Cualquier (before a noun) and cualquiera (alone) mean “any, whichever”. Quien and el que / los que / las que can mean “the one(s) who”. Lo que means “what, whatever”.

rows: Whoever wants to help can sign up.
Cualquier persona que necesite ayuda puede llamar.
Any person who needs help can call.
Los que tengan hambre pueden comer aquí.
Those who are hungry can eat here.
Cualquiera que sea la respuesta, la aceptaremos.
Whatever the answer is, we will accept it.

explanations.title: Compare with a known group
explanations.body: When you are describing a group that is actually there, the indicative is used.

examples.text: Los que tienen hambre ya están en la fila.
examples.translation: Those who are hungry are already in line.

examples.text: Los que tengan hambre mañana pueden venir a las ocho.
examples.translation: Those who are hungry tomorrow can come at eight.

examples.text: Lo que dices es verdad.
examples.translation: What you say is true.

examples.text: Lo que digas mañana será importante.
examples.translation: What you say tomorrow will be important.

exercises.prompt: Quien ___ ayudar mañana puede inscribirse en la lista.
exercises.promptTranslation: Whoever wants to help tomorrow can sign up on the list.

exercises.prompt: Cualquier persona que ___ ayuda puede llamar a este número.
exercises.promptTranslation: Any person who needs help can call this number.

exercises.prompt: Los que ___ hambre mañana pueden venir a las ocho.
exercises.explanation: Unknown people, in the future: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Those who are hungry tomorrow can come at eight.

exercises.prompt: Los que ___ hambre ahora ya están en la fila.
exercises.explanation: The group is in front of you now: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: Those who are hungry right now are already in line.

exercises.prompt: Haz lo que ___; nadie puede hacer más.
exercises.explanation: Whatever you are able to: subjunctive.
exercises.promptTranslation: Do what you can; nobody can do more.

exercises.prompt: Lo que ___ ahora es muy importante; por favor, escúchame.
exercises.explanation: What I am saying right now: indicative.
exercises.promptTranslation: What I am saying now is very important; please listen to me.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence talks about an open, unknown group?
options: Las personas que quieren ya vinieron.
El señor que quiere está aquí.
Mi tía, que quiere ayudar, vive aquí.
Cualquier persona que quiera puede venir.

exercises.prompt: What does “cualquiera” mean in “Cualquiera puede hacerlo”?
Which means “Whoever wants to come is welcome”?
exercises.explanation: Quien + subjunctive; agreement with a singular subject.

lessons.title: 641. Irregular subjunctive forms in descriptions: sea, esté, vaya, sepa, dé, haya
lessons.subtitle: Busco una casa que sea barata y que esté cerca del trabajo.

explanations.title: Six verbs that do not follow the yo rule
explanations.body: The present subjunctive normally starts from the yo form of the present. These six verbs are exceptions.

tables.note: The subjunctive of hay is haya: no creo que haya tiempo.

explanations.title: In descriptions
explanations.body: These forms often appear after que when you are describing something you are looking for.

examples.text: Busco una casa que sea barata y que esté cerca del trabajo.
examples.translation: I am looking for a house that is cheap and near work.

examples.text: Necesitamos un maestro que sepa explicar bien.

examples.text: Queremos un autobús que vaya directamente al hospital.
examples.translation: We want a bus that goes directly to the hospital.

examples.text: ¿Hay algún programa que dé comida a las familias?
examples.translation: Is there any program that gives food to families?

examples.text: No existe ningún lugar donde haya agua limpia.
examples.translation: There is no place where there is clean water.

exercises.prompt: Busco una casa que ___ barata; mi sueldo es muy bajo.
exercises.explanation: Ser describes the type of house; I don’t have one yet.
exercises.promptTranslation: I’m looking for a house that is cheap; my salary is very low.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want an apartment that is near the hospital.

exercises.promptTranslation: We need a teacher who knows how to explain mathematics well.

exercises.promptTranslation: We want a bus that goes directly to the hospital.

exercises.promptTranslation: Is there any program that gives food to poor families?

exercises.explanation: Estar de mi lado: be on my side; plural.

lessons.title: 642. Stem-changing verbs in descriptions: pueda, quiera, duerma, pida, vuelva
lessons.subtitle: Necesito un trabajo que me permita dormir bien y volver temprano.

explanations.title: The boot also appears here
explanations.body: Stem-changing verbs change in the subjunctive just like in the present. -ar and -er verbs change in the same persons as in the present (not nosotros or vosotros). -ir verbs also change in nosotros and vosotros: dormir → durmamos, pedir → pidamos.

explanations.title: In descriptions
explanations.body: These sentences describe something wished for or searched for.

examples.text: Necesito un trabajo que me permita volver temprano a casa.
examples.translation: I need a job that allows me to get home early.

examples.text: Buscamos una escuela donde los niños puedan jugar.
examples.translation: We are looking for a school where the children can play.

examples.text: Queremos un barrio donde se pueda dormir tranquilo.
examples.translation: We want a neighborhood where people can sleep peacefully.

examples.text: No conozco a nadie que pida más que ella.
examples.translation: I don’t know anyone who asks for more than she does.

exercises.prompt: Buscamos una escuela donde los niños ___ jugar y aprender.
exercises.promptTranslation: We are looking for a school where the children can play and learn.

exercises.prompt: Quiero un trabajo que me ___ volver temprano a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: I want a job that allows me to get home early.

exercises.prompt: Necesito una persona que ___ trabajar los sábados.
exercises.promptTranslation: I need a person who wants to work on Saturdays.

exercises.prompt: Buscamos un barrio donde nosotros ___ dormir tranquilos.

exercises.promptTranslation: We are looking for a neighborhood where we can sleep peacefully.

exercises.promptTranslation: There is no employee who asks for more help than Marcos.

exercises.prompt: Necesitamos un lugar donde los niños ___ jugar sin peligro.

exercises.promptTranslation: I want a life where I can return home without fear.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct nosotros subjunctive of dormir?
exercises.explanation: -ir verbs change o → u in nosotros.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct nosotros subjunctive of volver?
exercises.explanation: -er verbs keep the stem in nosotros.

lessons.title: 643. Classified ads and notices: Se busca una persona que…
lessons.subtitle: Se necesitan voluntarios que puedan ayudar los sábados.

explanations.title: Ads describe people and things that are still unknown
explanations.body: In job ads and notices, the writer is looking for someone or something that is not yet found, so the verb in the que clause is in the subjunctive. Ads that describe an existing offer use the indicative.

examples.text: Se necesitan voluntarios que puedan ayudar los sábados.

exercises.prompt: Se busca persona que ___ experiencia en atención al público.
exercises.explanation: The ad looks for an unknown person: subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Se necesitan voluntarios que ___ ayudar los sábados.
exercises.promptTranslation: Volunteers who can help on Saturdays are needed.

exercises.prompt: Se alquila apartamento que ___ a cinco minutos del metro.

exercises.prompt: Se vende una casa que ___ tres cuartos y un patio.
exercises.promptTranslation: A house that has three bedrooms and a yard is for sale.

lessons.title: 644. Verbs that work like gustar: faltar, sobrar, quedar, hacer falta, alcanzar
lessons.subtitle: Me falta tiempo. A los pueblos les faltan médicos.

explanations.title: The thing that is lacking is the subject
explanations.body: Like gustar, these verbs agree with the thing that is lacking, left over or needed (the subject), and the person who experiences it appears as an indirect object pronoun (me, te, le, nos, les). Because the subject is usually after the verb, the verb is plural when the noun is plural.

rows: I lack time. / I am short of time.
A los pueblos les faltan médicos.
Problems abound and solutions are missing.
Mi sueldo no me alcanza para pagar el alquiler.
My salary isn’t enough for me to pay the rent.

exercises.promptTranslation: Small towns lack doctors.

exercises.prompt: Me ___ tiempo para estudiar y trabajar.
exercises.promptTranslation: I lack time to study and work.

lessons.title: 645. Talking about lack: la falta de, carecer de, escaso, la escasez
lessons.subtitle: Algunas zonas carecen de agua limpia y de servicios médicos.

explanations.title: Six useful expressions about lack
explanations.body: Choose the pattern that fits the sentence. Notice the prepositions: la falta de, carecer de, escasez de, acceso a.

rows: La falta de agua limpia causa enfermedades.
Algunas zonas carecen de servicios médicos.
El agua es escasa en esa región.
Hay escasez de medicinas en el hospital.
Muchas familias no tienen acceso a internet.
El dinero no es suficiente para todos los gastos.

lessons.title: 646. Vocabulary: ethnic and religious groups

explanations.title: Respectful vocabulary
explanations.body: These words appear in news and in school texts. Terms for groups can differ from country to country, and many people prefer to describe themselves with their own words, so listen to how a person or community names itself.

of mixed ancestry (a historical term used differently in each country)

Una minoría puede tener menos poder político.

explanations.body: Tradición, lengua, idioma and cultura describe what a community shares.

lessons.title: 647. Reading: the diversity of Latin America
lessons.subtitle: En América Latina viven cientos de pueblos indígenas y muchas personas afrodescendientes.

explanations.title: A region of many peoples
explanations.body: This short reading summarizes facts that many reports describe. Figures change from year to year and from source to source, so the text speaks in general terms. Indigenous peoples, people of African descent and people of European and Asian origin all live in the region.

lessons.title: 648. Reading: hunger, prices and the basic basket
lessons.subtitle: Cuando suben los precios de los alimentos, muchas familias comen menos o comen peor.

explanations.title: Why do people go hungry?
explanations.body: Hunger has several causes, and experts discuss them. One useful term is la canasta básica: the group of foods and products that a family needs each month. When the cost of the canasta básica rises faster than salaries, many families cannot buy enough.

examples.text: La canasta básica es el conjunto de alimentos y productos que una familia necesita cada mes.
examples.translation: The canasta básica is the group of foods and products that a family needs each month.

examples.text: Cuando suben los precios de los alimentos, muchas familias comen menos o comen peor.
examples.translation: When food prices go up, many families eat less or eat worse.

examples.text: Una sequía, la inflación y la falta de empleo pueden aumentar el hambre.
examples.translation: A drought, inflation and lack of jobs can increase hunger.

examples.text: Algunos gobiernos dan ayudas en dinero o en comida a las familias más pobres.

lessons.title: 649. Reading: health and the two kinds of hospital

explanations.title: Public and private care
explanations.body: In many countries, people use two health systems: a public one, paid mostly with taxes, and a private one, paid by the patient or with private insurance. Differences in income often lead to differences in the quality and speed of care.

lessons.title: 651. Reading: women, work and violence (general facts)

explanations.title: A serious topic
explanations.body: This reading summarizes general facts that international organizations and national governments report. It does not name individuals, and statistics are not given because they vary by country, year and method of counting.

lessons.title: 652. El / la with a different meaning: policía, capital, orden, guía, modelo, corte, cura

explanations.title: Same word, different gender, different meaning
explanations.body: A few Spanish nouns change meaning when the article changes from el to la. The pairs below are neutral and common in news and daily life.

rows: the police force; also a female officer
a court of law; a royal court
tables.note: Other nouns change only by the person: el médico / la médica.

lessons.title: 653. Cause and effect: porque, ya que, debido a, por eso, así que
lessons.subtitle: Los precios subieron; por eso, muchas familias compran menos.

explanations.title: Linking a cause to a result
explanations.body: Some connectors introduce the cause, and some introduce the result. Debido a and a causa de are followed by a noun (before a conjugated verb, use debido a que or a causa de que), while porque and ya que are followed directly by a clause with a conjugated verb.

rows: the cause, with a noun (debido a que + verb)
the cause, with a noun (a causa de que + verb)
tables.note: Por qué is two words in questions; porque is one word in answers.

explanations.title: Examples
explanations.body: These examples show the connectors in use.

examples.text: Muchas familias compran menos porque los precios subieron.
examples.translation: Many families buy less because prices went up.

examples.translation: Prices went up; that is why many families buy less.

examples.text: Hubo menos empleo debido a la crisis.
examples.translation: There were fewer jobs due to the crisis.

examples.text: Ya que no había trabajo, muchos jóvenes se fueron.
examples.translation: Since there was no work, many young people left.

examples.text: La pobreza bajó; como resultado, más niños fueron a la escuela.
examples.translation: Poverty went down; as a result, more children went to school.

lessons.title: 654. Opinions about social problems: es importante que…, es evidente que…
lessons.subtitle: Es importante que el gobierno construya escuelas. Es evidente que la pobreza afecta a los niños.

explanations.title: Opinion or fact?
explanations.body: Impersonal expressions of value, need or doubt (es importante, es necesario, es urgente, es posible, es probable, es una lástima) are followed by the subjunctive. Expressions that state certainty or truth (es evidente, es verdad, es cierto, es obvio) are followed by the indicative.

rows: Es importante que el gobierno construya escuelas.
Es evidente que la pobreza afecta a los niños.
Es necesario que todos tengan agua limpia.
Es verdad que los precios subieron.
Es urgente que los hospitales reciban medicinas.
Es cierto que hay menos empleo.
Es posible que la situación mejore.
Es obvio que hace falta ayuda.

explanations.title: Notes
explanations.body: No es verdad que and no es cierto que deny a statement and are usually followed by the subjunctive: No es verdad que no haya soluciones. Es una lástima que expresses a reaction and also takes the subjunctive.

examples.text: Es necesario que los jóvenes tengan empleo.
examples.translation: It is necessary for young people to have jobs.

examples.text: Es probable que el desempleo baje el próximo año.
examples.translation: It is likely that unemployment will drop next year.

examples.text: Es una lástima que tantos niños pasen hambre.
examples.translation: It is a shame that so many children go hungry.

examples.text: Es evidente que la situación es difícil.
examples.translation: It is clear that the situation is difficult.

to arrive in a country to live there

explanations.body: The meaning of these words depends on the law of each country, but the basic ideas are widely shared. Note: many organizations recommend persona indocumentada rather than the adjective ilegal applied to a person, because a person is not “illegal”; an action can be.

explanations.title: Words around the border
explanations.body: A border is a place where a country ends. Governments handle it in different ways: with physical barriers, with inspections, or with shelters for people who arrive.

El muro tiene muchos kilómetros de largo.

caravan: a group that travels together

En el paso fronterizo hay un control de documentos.

explanations.title: Two views
explanations.body: People disagree about walls and fences. Some governments say that barriers protect security. Critics say that barriers push people toward more dangerous routes. Neither claim is a simple fact; reports and experts offer different evidence.

explanations.body: Huir, atravesar and acoger have small spelling changes in some forms. Atravesar changes e → ie. Huir adds y in several forms (huyo, huyes, huye, huyen). Acoger changes the g to j in the yo form (acojo).

lessons.title: 660. Reading: why do people migrate?

explanations.title: Push and pull
explanations.body: Experts often separate the reasons that push people away from home (violence, war, poverty, disasters) from the reasons that pull them toward another place (jobs, family, schools, safety). Many migrants have a mix of reasons.

explanations.title: Four groups of triggers
explanations.body: Emotion (me alegra que, temo que, siento que), doubt (dudo que, no creo que), denial (niego que, no es verdad que) and impersonal expressions of value (es urgente que, es importante que) take the subjunctive. The affirmative of certainty (no dudo que, creo que, es verdad que) takes the indicative.

El presidente no niega que hay escasez.

lessons.title: 663. Hope and probability: ojalá, tal vez, quizás, puede que, a lo mejor
lessons.subtitle: Ojalá que todo salga bien. A lo mejor llegamos mañana.

explanations.title: Hoping and guessing
explanations.body: Ojalá (que) expresses a wish and is always followed by the subjunctive. Puede que, tal vez and quizás/quizá express possibility. Puede que always takes the subjunctive. Tal vez and quizás usually take the subjunctive when the speaker feels real doubt, and the indicative is possible when the speaker thinks it is probable. A lo mejor is different: it is always followed by the indicative.

lessons.title: 666. Time and conditions: antes de que, sin que

explanations.title: Before and without
explanations.body: Antes de que and sin que are always followed by the subjunctive. Their prepositions (antes de, sin) are followed by an infinitive when the subject does not change.

Voy a comer antes de que Juan llegue.
Sale sin que nadie lo vea.

Cruza la calle sin que sus padres lo sepan.

explanations.title: Examples

lessons.title: 667. Conditions: a menos que, con tal de que, en caso de que
lessons.subtitle: Te ayudaré con tal de que me avises. No iré a menos que me llamen.

explanations.title: Three conjunctions of condition
explanations.body: A menos que = unless. Con tal de que = provided that. En caso de que = in case. All three are always followed by the subjunctive. Con tal de que is also heard as con tal que, and en caso de que is sometimes shortened to en caso que in everyday speech. The forms taught here (a menos que, con tal de que, en caso de que) are the safest.

rows: No iré a menos que me llamen.
Te ayudaré con tal de que me avises.
Lleva un suéter en caso de que haga frío.

explanations.title: More examples
explanations.body: The two clauses always have clear subjects.

explanations.title: When the action hasn’t happened yet
explanations.body: After cuando, use the subjunctive when the action is still in the future. Use the indicative when the action is habitual, happening now, or already happened. The tense of the main clause is the clue.

exercises.promptTranslation: When I was little, I lived in a town.

lessons.title: 671. Future time: en cuanto, tan pronto como, después de que, hasta que
lessons.subtitle: Te lo diré en cuanto lo sepa. No saldremos hasta que termine la lluvia.

explanations.title: More time conjunctions
explanations.body: These conjunctions work like cuando: subjunctive for a pending future event, indicative for habitual or past events.

rows: Te lo diré en cuanto lo sepa.
Te llamaré tan pronto como llegue.
Cenaremos después de que lleguen los niños.
No saldremos hasta que termine la lluvia.

explanations.title: The same conjunctions in other tenses
explanations.body: Compare the future with the past and with a habit.

examples.text: Ayer salimos en cuanto terminó la lluvia.
examples.translation: Yesterday we left as soon as the rain finished.

examples.text: Siempre salimos en cuanto termina la lluvia.
examples.translation: We always leave as soon as the rain finishes.

examples.text: Esperé hasta que llegó el último autobús.
examples.translation: I waited until the last bus arrived.

examples.text: Esperaré hasta que llegue el último autobús.
examples.translation: I will wait until the last bus arrives.

exercises.prompt: Te lo diré en cuanto lo ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: I’ll tell you as soon as I know it.

exercises.prompt: Cenaremos después de que ___ los niños.
exercises.promptTranslation: We’ll have dinner after the children arrive.

exercises.prompt: No saldremos hasta que ___ la lluvia.
exercises.promptTranslation: We won’t leave until the rain ends.

exercises.prompt: Ayer esperé hasta que ___ el último autobús.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday I waited until the last bus arrived.

exercises.prompt: Siempre pago la cuenta tan pronto como la ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: I always pay the bill as soon as I receive it.

exercises.prompt: Mañana pagaré la cuenta tan pronto como la ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow I’ll pay the bill as soon as I receive it.

exercises.prompt: Hoy esperaremos aquí hasta que nos ___ la respuesta.
exercises.promptTranslation: Today we will wait here until they give us the answer.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence describes a habit?
options: Saldremos en cuanto termine la lluvia.
Saldríamos en cuanto terminara la lluvia.
Siempre salimos en cuanto termina la lluvia.
Ayer salimos en cuanto terminó la lluvia.

exercises.prompt: What does “hasta que” mean?

lessons.title: 672. Even if and even though: aunque
lessons.subtitle: Aunque hoy llueve, salimos. Aunque mañana llueva, saldremos.

explanations.title: Fact or possibility
explanations.body: Aunque + indicative introduces a fact: although, even though. Aunque + subjunctive usually introduces a possibility or something not yet true: even if.

rows: Aunque el viaje es caro, voy.
Aunque el viaje sea caro, iré.

explanations.title: Notice the clue
explanations.body: Time words and the main verb help you choose: hoy and the present point to a fact; mañana and the future point to a possibility.

examples.text: Aunque hoy llueve, salimos para la reunión.
examples.translation: Even though it is raining today, we are going out for the meeting.

examples.text: Aunque mañana llueva, saldremos para la reunión.
examples.translation: Even if it rains tomorrow, we will go out for the meeting.

examples.text: Aunque no tengo mucho dinero, ayudo a mi familia.
examples.translation: Although I don’t have much money, I help my family.

examples.text: Aunque no tenga mucho dinero el próximo año, ayudaré a mi familia.
examples.translation: Even if I don’t have much money next year, I will help my family.

exercises.promptTranslation: Although it is raining a lot today, we are going out for the meeting.

exercises.prompt: Aunque mañana ___ mucho, saldremos para la reunión.
exercises.promptTranslation: Even if it rains a lot tomorrow, we will go out for the meeting.

exercises.promptTranslation: Although I don’t have much money now, I help my family.

exercises.prompt: Aunque el próximo año no ___ mucho dinero, ayudaré a mi familia.
exercises.promptTranslation: Even if I don’t have much money next year, I will help my family.

exercises.prompt: Aunque el viaje ___ caro, iré con mi hermano. Todavía no sé el precio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Even if the trip is expensive, I’ll go with my brother. I don’t know the price yet.

exercises.prompt: Aunque el viaje ___ caro, iré con mi hermano. Ya vi el precio.
exercises.promptTranslation: Although the trip is expensive, I’ll go with my brother. I’ve already seen the price.

exercises.prompt: What does “aunque” mean with the indicative?
What does “aunque” mean with the subjunctive?
Which sentence means “Even if it is expensive, I will buy it” (we don’t know the price)?

lessons.title: 673. Giving directions: sigue derecho hasta que…, dobla cuando…
lessons.subtitle: Sigue derecho hasta que veas la iglesia. Dobla a la izquierda después de que pases el banco.

explanations.title: Directions are future events
explanations.body: When you give directions, you describe actions that the listener will do later. That is why the subjunctive appears after hasta que, cuando, después de que, en cuanto and tan pronto como.

rows: Sigue derecho hasta que veas la iglesia.
Go straight until you see the church.
Dobla a la izquierda después de que pases el banco.
Turn left after you pass the bank.
Cruza la plaza cuando llegues a la esquina.
Cross the square when you reach the corner.
Call me as soon as you arrive.
Camina hasta que encuentres un parque.
Walk until you find a park.

exercises.prompt: Sigue derecho hasta que ___ la iglesia.
exercises.promptTranslation: Go straight until you see the church.

exercises.prompt: Dobla a la izquierda después de que ___ el banco.
exercises.promptTranslation: Turn left after you pass the bank.

exercises.prompt: Cruza la plaza cuando ___ a la esquina.
exercises.promptTranslation: Cross the square when you reach the corner.

exercises.promptTranslation: Call me as soon as you arrive at the station.

exercises.prompt: Camina hasta que ___ un parque.
exercises.promptTranslation: Walk until you find a park.

exercises.prompt: Señor, siga derecho hasta que ___ el banco.
exercises.promptTranslation: Sir, go straight until you see the bank.

exercises.prompt: Señores, doblen a la derecha cuando ___ al semáforo.
exercises.promptTranslation: Ladies and gentlemen, turn right when you reach the traffic light.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Camina hasta que encuentras la plaza.
Camina hasta que encuentres la plaza.
Camina hasta que encontrar la plaza.

exercises.prompt: Why are directions often in the subjunctive after cuando or hasta que?
options: They describe actions the listener will do in the future

lessons.title: 674. Indicative or subjunctive? Time conjunctions in the past, the present and the future
lessons.subtitle: Ayer llegué y comí. Siempre como cuando llego. Mañana comeré cuando llegue.

explanations.title: The main clause is the clue
explanations.body: Look at the main clause before the conjunction: a past or habitual action leads to the indicative; a future action or a command leads to the subjunctive.

exercises.prompt: Ayer comí cuando ___ a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Yesterday I ate when I got home.

exercises.prompt: Siempre como cuando ___ a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: I always eat when I get home.

exercises.prompt: Mañana comeré cuando ___ a casa.
exercises.promptTranslation: Tomorrow I’ll eat when I get home.

exercises.prompt: Espera aquí hasta que yo ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: Wait here until I come back.

exercises.prompt: Esperé aquí hasta que ella ___.
exercises.promptTranslation: I waited here until she came back.

exercises.promptTranslation: Every day I work until night comes.

lessons.title: 675. Duration and ongoing action: llevar, andar, seguir, ir, venir + gerund
lessons.subtitle: Llevo dos años viviendo aquí. Mi hermano anda buscando trabajo.

explanations.title: Five verbs that take the gerund
explanations.body: Several verbs combine with the gerund (-ando, -iendo) to show how an action develops over time.

rows: to have been doing something for…
to be going around doing something
to have been doing up to now

explanations.title: The gerund forms
explanations.body: Regular gerunds: -ar → -ando, -er/-ir → -iendo. After a vowel, -iendo becomes -yendo: leer → leyendo, construir → construyendo. Pedir and decir change the stem: pidiendo, diciendo.

examples.text: Mi hermano lleva tres meses buscando trabajo.
examples.translation: My brother has been looking for work for three months.

examples.text: Mis padres siguen viviendo en el pueblo.
examples.translation: My parents are still living in the town.

examples.text: La situación va mejorando poco a poco.
examples.translation: The situation is getting better little by little.

examples.text: Ando buscando un apartamento cerca del trabajo.
examples.translation: I am out looking for an apartment near work.

exercises.promptTranslation: I have been living here for two years.

exercises.prompt: Mi hermano anda ___ trabajo en la ciudad.

exercises.promptTranslation: My parents are still living in the same neighborhood.

exercises.promptTranslation: She is improving her Spanish little by little.

lessons.title: 676. Reading: Hispanics and Latinos in the United States
lessons.subtitle: Millones de personas de origen hispano viven en los Estados Unidos.

explanations.title: A large and varied community
explanations.body: The word hispano is used for people with roots in Spain or Latin America, and latino mostly for people with roots in Latin America. People do not all prefer the same word, and many describe themselves by their family’s country: mexicano-americano, cubano-americano, dominicano and so on. This reading summarizes general facts that are reported by official counts.

examples.text: En los Estados Unidos viven decenas de millones de personas de origen hispano o latino.
examples.translation: Tens of millions of people of Hispanic or Latino origin live in the United States.

examples.text: Según los censos, es uno de los grupos más grandes del país y representa aproximadamente a una de cada cinco personas.
examples.translation: According to the censuses, it is one of the largest groups in the country and represents roughly one in five people.

examples.text: La mayoría de estas personas nació en los Estados Unidos.
examples.translation: Most of these people were born in the United States.

examples.text: Los orígenes son muy variados: México, Puerto Rico, Cuba, El Salvador, la República Dominicana y muchos otros países.
examples.translation: The origins are very varied: Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic and many other countries.

examples.text: Los puertorriqueños son ciudadanos estadounidenses desde que nacen.
examples.translation: Puerto Ricans are U.S. citizens from birth.

examples.text: En muchos hogares se habla español, inglés o los dos idiomas.
examples.translation: In many homes people speak Spanish, English or both languages.

examples.text: Algunas personas dicen que el bilingüismo es una riqueza; otras piensan que todos deben aprender inglés lo antes posible.
examples.translation: Some people say bilingualism is an asset; others think that everyone should learn English as soon as possible.

exercises.prompt: What do “hispano” and “latino” refer to?
options: Only people who speak Spanish at work
People with roots in Spain or Latin America
exercises.explanation: Raíces en España o América Latina.

exercises.prompt: According to the reading, where were most of these people born?
exercises.explanation: La mayoría nació en los Estados Unidos.

exercises.prompt: What does the reading say about Puerto Ricans?
options: They are U.S. citizens from birth

exercises.prompt: Según los censos, es uno de los grupos más ___ del país.
exercises.promptTranslation: According to the censuses, it is one of the largest groups in the country.

exercises.promptTranslation: The origins are very varied: Mexico, Puerto Rico, Cuba and many other countries.

exercises.prompt: En muchos hogares se habla español, inglés o los ___ idiomas.
exercises.promptTranslation: In many homes people speak Spanish, English or both languages.

exercises.prompt: What do some people say about bilingualism?
What do others think?
options: That everyone should learn English as soon as possible
exercises.explanation: Otras piensan que todos deben aprender inglés.
